concepts.name: Weil positivity criterion
concepts.plain: A quadratic form built from primes, the archimedean place and the pole. RH holds exactly when it is never negative.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: Weil 1952: RH ⇔ W(f∗f̃*) ≥ 0 for all test f; equivalently the Hermitian form 𝒬 is positive, ⇔ a unitary Hilbert realization of the scaling flow (TAA Lemma 1 Thm 2.1 (iv)).
pitfalls: The zero-side check is tautological (TAA Lemma 142); only the prime side with no zeros is a test.
"Q = LP + positive" is false (TAA Lemma 8).
Definition, not source (TAA Lemma 152 §3): Weil's criterion ⇔ RH, so it cannot by itself supply the positivity.

rels.note: TAA Lemma 142: Weil form = relative intersection matrix on translates

concepts.name: ψ(x) − x (explicit formula, deviation from the pole)
concepts.plain: Count prime powers with weight log p and subtract the pole’s prediction x; what remains is a sum over zeros. RH ⇔ the remainder is O(√x log²x).
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: Explicit formula ψ(x) = x − Σ_ρ x^ρ/ρ − log 2π − ½log(1 − x⁻²); RH ⇔ ψ(x) − x = O(x^{½+ε}). In TAA the x term is the pole/𝕃 reference; ψ − x ≠ 0 measures the flow-relative H¹.
concepts.uncertain: The explicit-formula wording is standard (cited), not from a specific lemma section.
pitfalls: ψ(x) − x ≠ 0 is not a failure: it is the zero contribution relative to the pole reference.

rels.note: both compare a prime product/sum to a pole reference
[less-sensitive-than] Gram separates DH at span 3.85; ψ separation needs log x ≳ 8 (TAA Lemma 149)

concepts.name: Connes trace formula
aliases: Connes cokernel: positive space sees only critical zeros; RH ⇔ global trace formula
concepts.plain: Connes’ trace formula on the adele class space: zeros appear as an absorption spectrum, and the global trace formula holding is equivalent to RH.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: Connes 1999 (read at source, TAA Lemma 30/TAA Lemma 71): global trace formula ≡ RH; Thm 1 sees only critical zeros (δ > 1); Thm 5 char p; zeros = absorption spectrum (TAA Lemma 71). TAA Lemma 82: cutoff, non-critical zeros as resonances. TAA Lemma 118: Connes reduces RH for Hecke L to the trace formula ⇒ Weil positivity; absorption spectrum ghost-blind. TAA Lemma 138 R2: Hilbert–Pólya positivity is circular if the inner product is Weil’s form. TAA Lemma 151: Connes's cokernel L²(C_k)/Im E (absorption spectrum) is the MP1 candidate; E carries |g|^{½} (canonical real half twist); C ⊕ C(1) boundary = H⁰/H². Missing on both sides: MP4. TAA Lemma 153 (E, corrected per H): Selecta Math. (N.S.) 5 (1999) 29–106, doi 10.1007/s000290050042 (Crossref; abstract re-read). Connes cokernel: the positive (Hilbert) space sees only the critical zeros — spectral realization of the critical zeros as an absorption spectrum (δ > 1 version, Thm 1 as read at source in TAA Lemma 30/TAA Lemma 71), noncritical zeros only as resonances; semi-local trace formula proved; RH ⇔ validity of the global trace formula (⇔ Weil positivity). A quotient of a Hilbert space is automatically positive, so 'positivity of the inherited form ⇔ RH' was wrong (TAA Lemma 153, correction 18): RH ⇔ nothing is missing from the positive space. The two quotients: (1) by ℚ^× acting on ideles → C_ℚ = 𝔸^×/ℚ^× (modular analogue Γ∖ℍ); (2) the cokernel of the summation map E (modular analogue: the constant term at the cusp; cusp forms = its kernel). CM points are not the quotient.

rels.note: RH ⇔ nothing missing from the positive space

concepts.name: Frobenius-graph lattice on E×E (relative counts = intersections with Δ)
concepts.plain: On the square of an elliptic curve, the graph of Frobenius meets the diagonal in the point count; the sign pattern of these intersections is exactly the Riemann hypothesis for the curve.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: e₁, e₂, Δ, Γ_{F^n} on E×E/F_q: Γ_n·e₁ = 1, Γ_n·e₂ = q^n, Δ·Γ_n = N_n, Γ_m·Γ_n = q^{min}N_{|m−n|}; complement Gram −[[2,a],[a,2q]] = −2 deg(m+nF); det = −(4q − a²); Hodge index ⇔ signature (1,3) ⇔ Hasse. NUM 11a1, 15 primes: (1,3,0), with Γ₂ (1,3,1); fake a > 2√p → (2,2). TAA Lemma 152 Prop 4.1 (NUM, zeta-free): 11a1, brute-force counts over F_{p^k} (p^k ≤ 729; p = 2,3,5,7,13,17,19) satisfy Γ_m·Γ_n = q^m N_{n−m} (incl. m = n, N₀ = 2 − 2g); Gram of ⟨e₁,e₂,Γ₀..Γ_K⟩ rank 4, inertia (1,3) exactly; fakes (5,5),(7,6),(13,8),(2,3) give (2,2). Prop 4.3: D_m·D_n = −Σ αᵢⁿβᵢᵐ.

rels.note: Rosati form = intersection form on the Frobenius plane

concepts.name: Definite cup square / Krein one-liner
concepts.plain: Positivity is put in by a definite Hermitian square: a flow that scales it forces every eigenvalue onto the line, and only null vectors (ghosts) can escape.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: If ⟨φᵗx, φᵗy⟩ = eᵗ⟨x,y⟩ for a Hermitian form, an eigenvector with eigenvalue e^{tρ} has Re ρ = ½ or is null; ρ pairs only with 1 − ρ̄ (Krein-neutral (1,1) block); definite ⇒ all on the line (TAA Lemma 152 Prop 2.1; NUM 2.3e−16). A bilinear cup pairing only pairs ρ with 1 − ρ (= functional equation, ghost-blind; Cor 2.2): Hermitian needs conjugation + Weil operator/polarization. Over F_q: the definite form is the Rosati trace form on End⁰(J)⊗ℝ (ππ′ = q ⇒ |σ(π)|² = q), equivalently Hodge index on NS(C×C) — not a Hermitian form on H¹_ét (TAA Lemma 152, correction 1). For ζ: MP4 (TAA Lemma 151), the only positivity input. On E×E the projection D_n = Γ_n − qⁿe₁ − e₂ gives D_m·D_n = −Σ αᵢⁿ βᵢᵐ, β = q/α: Hermitian iff |α| = √q (TAA Lemma 152 Prop 4.3).
pitfalls: Over F_q there is no positive Hermitian form on H¹_ét (TAA Lemma 152, correction 1).
A bilinear (cup) pairing gives only the FE (TAA Lemma 152, correction 2).

concepts.name: Lagarias/Hinkkanen criterion
concepts.plain: RH ⇔ the log-derivative of ξ has positive real part to the right of the line.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: Lagarias 1999 (1.5), credited to Hinkkanen: RH ⇔ Re ξ′/ξ(s) > 0 on Re s > ½ (TAA Lemmas 17, 146).

concepts.name: Primitive part V₀ = U^⊥
concepts.plain: What is left after removing the reference plane; on it the form should be negative (curves: theorem; ℚ: RH).
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: D° = D − d₁f₂ − d₂f₁; (D°)² = −Tr_{H¹}(α_Dα_D†) (TAA Lemma 133). Over ℚ V₀ = U^⊥ and D·D ≤ 0 on V₀ ⇔ RH (TAA Lemma 91).
numbers: λ_max on ker P / λ_max = 1.19–6361 over spans ≤ 16; 1.2–4.4 for L ≥ 12
pitfalls: A “−2Tr” formula holds only on the primitive part.

concepts.name: Missing: Deninger's conjectured cohomology for Spec ℤ, stated as axioms MP0–MP4 (no coined name)
concepts.plain: For ℚ both cohomologies we can compute vanish (étale H¹ = 0, Arakelov Pic⁰ = a point), yet ψ(x) − x ≠ 0. The zeros need a cohomology relative to the scaling flow.
concepts.label: Open
concepts.core: Construct the middle term of Tate's split at |x| = 1 as an H¹ for Spec ℤ carrying (a) a Frobenius-type flow whose spectrum is the zeros (MP1–MP2; needs the Euler product, absent for DH) and (b) a cup product H¹ × H¹ → H² ≅ ℝ(−1) (MP3; absent for DH), and prove the cup square definite on the primitive part (MP4 = Hodge index/Rosati sign; the only positivity input). MP0: H⁰/H² = Tate boundary terms f(0), f̂(0) (DH: none). Deninger's axioms, TAA refinements MP0/MP4 (TAA Lemma 151 Conj 4.1). TAA Lemma 153: Connes's cokernel (TAA Lemma 153, correction 18) — its Hilbert space is automatically positive and sees only critical zeros; RH ⇔ nothing missing ⇔ global trace formula. Recorded as a precision of MP4, no new missing piece (MPU153).
concepts.formula: N_n − (1 + qⁿ) = −Tr(Fⁿ | H¹) ↔ ψ(x) − x = −Σ_ρ x^ρ/ρ + …
concepts.proved: π₁ét(Spec ℤ) = 1 ⇒ H¹ét = 0 (TAA Lemma 140); curve row: N_n − (qⁿ + 1) = −Tr(Fⁿ | H¹) with relative Gram NSD (TAA Lemma 141 §1); Tr ↔ −(ψ − x) up to the s = 0 term and ARCH (TAA Lemma 142 corrections).
concepts.tests: Must carry a positive structure (Ax2), not only the trace formula: the explicit formula alone is ghost-blind in data (TAA Lemma 143: ghost defect ≤ 1.9e−5, 0.08× noise).

concepts.name: Missing: a Néron–Severi strictly larger than U containing the Frobenius classes Ψ_λ
concepts.plain: An intersection theory on the square in which the Connes–Consani correspondences Ψ_λ are genuine classes outside the pole plane U, with enough sections that their growth sees s(f,f).
concepts.label: Open
concepts.core: Need NS ⊋ U with Ψ_λ, and #H⁰(±nD(f)) ≥ 2^{n² s(f,f)/2} (TAA Lemma 147). Decisive missing objects: H¹ on the square, an intersection theory putting Ψ_λ into an NS larger than U, and quadratic RR (TAA Lemma 147 (iv)).
concepts.proved: Laurent piece of HZ ∧_𝕊 HZ: box count 2n² + 4n exact, but the quadratic coefficient 2αβ is the U-form ⇒ vacuous on degree-0 D(f) (TAA Lemma 147 Thm vac).
concepts.tests: Quadratic growth must come from V₀ = U^⊥, not from U (Thm vac). Ghost-sensitive side is s(f,f), which must be negative for ζ and fail for DH (TAA Lemma 142, TAA Lemma 147).
pitfalls: TAA Lemma 150 Prop 2.3: classes at log n (n ≤ 90, disjoint hats) are ghost-blind — ζ, DH and inserted ghosts all give λ_max < 0; NS ⊋ U must use continuous translates or all ratios λ ∈ ℚ₊ (PSI-2).

concepts.name: Missing: arithmetic Castelnuovo object (positive involution on a space where the Weil distribution is a |·|²)
concepts.plain: A space with an infinite H¹, a positive involution † and a flow u_t with u_t u_t† = eᵗ, on which the explicit-formula (Weil) distribution becomes a squared norm, with that positivity proved without using the zeros.
concepts.label: Open
concepts.core: Arithmetic Castelnuovo object = (C1) infinite H¹, (C2) positive involution, (C3) u_t u_t† = eᵗ, (C4) positivity proved without zeros (TAA Lemma 136); equivalently a positive involution plus a Frobenius-type flow with positivity proved without zeros (TAA Lemma 136 synthesis). Hilbert–Pólya form: a positive V ≅ H¹ (TAA Lemma 115); “all that is missing is an appropriate inner product” (Lax–Phillips, TAA Lemma 105/TAA Lemma 141).
concepts.proved: Over F_q: Ax2 ∧ Ax3 ⇔ |α| = √q (TAA Lemma 137, theorem). Over ℚ: isometry of the flow is unconditional (TAA Lemma 1); the Čech 2-class supplies C2–C3 structure but not the sign (TAA Lemma 138); Ax2 alone holds for fakes, Ax3 alone is tautological (TAA Lemma 137).
concepts.tests: Must separate ghosts: Ax2 and Ax3 jointly, never one alone (TAA Lemma 137). Must not define the inner product by Weil’s form (circular, TAA Lemma 138 R2; TAA Lemma 106).

concepts.name: Missing: H¹ on the square of the scaling site (Connes–Consani s(f,f) ≤ 0)
concepts.plain: A first cohomology on the square of Connes–Consani’s scaling site; with it, an RR theorem would give D(f)•D(f) ≤ 0, which is RH.
concepts.label: Open
concepts.core: CC18: RH ⇔ s(f,f) ≤ 0, s(f,f) = D•D with D = ∫fΨ_λ; five steps, only step 1 (complex lift) built; H¹ on the square of the scaling site, and hence RR there, is open (TAA Lemma 147, correction 2). ½D(f)•D(f) = ½s(f,f) is the Weil form (TAA Lemma 142).
concepts.proved: No RR for C_ℚ × C_ℚ exists (TAA Lemma 147, correction 2). The square exists as a site with Ψ_λ (TAA Lemma 30) but carries no H¹, RR or Hodge index (TAA Lemma 65).
concepts.tests: All H⁰-side objects built from ℤ ⊂ 𝔸_ℚ are ghost-blind; the topological side s(f,f) is ghost-sensitive (DH-location ghost positive from L* = 3.45, actual DH from 4.70) (TAA Lemma 142, TAA Lemma 147).

concepts.name: Missing: surface + ample class + Riemann–Roch for Spec ℤ (D8)
concepts.plain: The top substantive direction: a surface S over Spec ℤ with an ample class and a Riemann–Roch whose χ(nD) is quadratic, so that Hodge index follows as it does for curves.
concepts.label: Open
concepts.core: D8: surface + ample + RR for Spec ℤ — find S with χ(nD) quadratic and a Hodge index; obstacle: the collapse ℤ ⊗ ℤ = ℤ; sign = Weil form (TAA Lemma 140, TAA Lemma 141). Acceptance test (TAA Lemma 141): reconstruct the relative space and its form from independent constraints — (a) the hyperbolic plane U = ⟨𝟙, 𝕃⟩, (b) the scaling flow acting on it as diag(1, eᵗ), (c) ampleness at ∞, (d) RR/GRR with quadratic growth — then prove negativity on U^⊥. Any proof that uses the zeros, or defines the form by its negativity, fails. TAA Lemma 152: phrased as a 'degree' — a count (≥ 0) on arithmetic correspondences whose polarization is Weil's form; in Cayley–Klein terms the absolute of the arithmetic pairing must be imaginary (= MP4).
concepts.proved: Over F_q: surface + ample + RR ⇒ Hodge index (Segre 1937, Grothendieck 1958) (TAA Lemma 140). Spec ℤ ×_ℤ Spec ℤ = Spec ℤ (TAA Lemma 65). Arithmetic surfaces (curve × Spec O_K) satisfy V1–V3, but the relative part is Néron–Tate, not ζ (TAA Lemma 145).
concepts.tests: Must pass the tautology test (no zeros, no definition by negativity, TAA Lemma 141) and the must-fail-for-DH test (TAA Lemma 147).

concepts.name: Missing: quadratic Riemann–Roch + “ampleness ⇒ effectivity” on the square
concepts.plain: A Riemann–Roch on Spec ℤ × Spec ℤ whose Euler characteristic is quadratic in D, together with the step “ample ⇒ has sections ⇒ effective”. This is exactly the part of the curve proof that Spec ℤ lacks.
concepts.label: Open
concepts.core: Classical chain: S1 quadratic RR, S2 Serre duality, S3 h¹ ≥ 0 / Minkowski, S4 sections ⇒ effective, S5 ample·effective > 0. Missing Spec ℤ step = quadratic S1 + S4 (“ampleness ⇒ effectivity” via a 2-dim h⁰) (TAA Lemma 145 V3, verdict VF-E). Parity: quadratic χ is even in D, linear χ odd ⇒ fixed rank proves only degree c(D) = 0, never sees D².
concepts.uncertain: The displayed “needed shape” is the classical surface RR, quoted as the target form.
concepts.proved: Every proved Connes–Consani RR is 1-dimensional, χ = deg + const (TAA Lemma 147); fixed-rank products are linear, h⁰/n = 2.000 at n = 400 (TAA Lemma 145 Thm linear); on ℙ¹_ℤ χ̂ is quadratic and realizes the U-form (TAA Lemma 145). Hodge index also needs S2, S3, S5 (TAA Lemma 145 corrections).
concepts.tests: Must fail for Davenport–Heilbronn, hence must use the Euler product (TAA Lemma 147, necessary condition). Must see D², i.e. be quadratic. V3 on the square ⇔ Weil ⇔ RH, so it must be proved, not assumed (TAA Lemma 145).

concepts.name: Missing: an inequality consequence of automorphy (SC-E / HS-1)
concepts.plain: Automorphy (invariance under the full modular group) decides where the zeros are but does not derive it; what is missing is an inequality that automorphy forces on δ_ρ.
concepts.label: Open
concepts.core: SC-E (structural P: Hecke/Euler product) = Selberg-class RH, the open non-circular version of trapped-set rigidity (TAA Lemma 143); sharpened to “an inequality consequence of automorphy” (→ Weil positivity, TAA Lemma 142) (TAA Lemma 144). HS-1: an automorphy-defect functional 𝒟(Λ_X) ≥ 0 with 𝒟 = 0 ⇔ Λ_X = ξ; it needs an inequality that the defect forces on δ_ρ, which we do not have (TAA Lemma 144).
concepts.proved: Thm 3.3 (TAA Lemma 144): automorphy picks a = 1/ξ(2s), c = φ uniquely, exact defect formula; Hecke alone puts no constraint on φ (Prop 3.2). SC-A ⇔ RH (restatement); SC-B false (DH); SC-C false (all cofinite Γ); HS-B (Hecke + unitarity ⇒ δ = 0) false (fakes).
concepts.tests: Fakes pass Hecke/FE/Δ/unitarity to 1e−25 but fail S-invariance: DH by 1.4–3.2%, the degree-0 ghost by 4.5e−6–1.6e−4 (TAA Lemma 144). The inequality must be violated by both.

concepts.name: Missing: a BRST-type complex Q with H(Q) = U^⊥ positive (PM-3)
concepts.plain: A nilpotent operator on the test functions whose cohomology is exactly the relative space U^⊥, so that “remove the pole plane, then the rest is positive” becomes a cohomology statement, as in Gupta–Bleuler/BRST.
concepts.label: Open
concepts.core: PM-3: Gupta–Bleuler/BRST complex Q on TAA Lemma 142’s test functions with H(Q) = U^⊥ (TAA Lemma 146). Thm gb (linear algebra, proved): for V = U ⊕ U^⊥, U = ⟨F₁, F₂⟩, F_i² = 0, F₁F₂ = 1, the quotient F₁^⊥/⟨F₁⟩ is isometric to U^⊥; a nilpotent Q with cohomology U^⊥ would package it as a flow-relative cohomology (Open).
concepts.proved: TAA Lemma 115: BRST structure exact over F_q and ℚ; “no ghosts” ⇔ RH (restatement); missing positive V ≅ H¹ (Hilbert–Pólya). TAA Lemma 146: the BRST quartet decouples, but a ghost quartet survives.
concepts.tests: A ghost quartet is exactly a quartet that fails to decouple (TAA Lemma 146); the complex must not decouple it. Positivity of the quotient is an input in QED and is RH for ζ.

concepts.name: Missing: passivity of ξ′/ξ from a zero-free mechanism (Lagarias margin)
concepts.plain: RH is equivalent to ξ′/ξ being a passive (positive-real) response to the right of the line. What is missing is a proof of a passivity margin that uses only primes, the pole and the archimedean place.
concepts.label: Open
concepts.core: Lagarias (1.5), attributed to Hinkkanen: RH ⇔ Re ξ′/ξ(s) > 0 on Re s > ½ (TAA Lemma 146, opened). PM-1: a Lagarias margin h(σ) for ξ vs DH/ghost — a provable, ghost-sensitive passivity margin? (TAA Lemma 146).
concepts.formula: RH ⇔ Re ξ′/ξ(s) > 0 for Re s > ½
concepts.proved: Re ξ′/ξ = Σ(σ−β)/((σ−β)² + (t−γ)²): each zero an absorption line, an off-line zero a gain line (TAA Lemma 146). Passivity ⇒ causality, not conversely (TAA Lemma 146 corrections). Free positivity (Λ(n) ≥ 0, KMS, Bagchi recurrence) is ghost-blind (TAA Lemma 136, TAA Lemma 118).
concepts.tests: Grid σ ∈ [.505, 1.1], t ∈ [80, 92]: ξ min +0.00467; DH −66.84 at (0.794, 85.70), 1.89% negative; ghost −66.97, 1.94% (TAA Lemma 146). The margin must stay positive for ξ and go negative for both.

concepts.name: Missing: RR/GRR on an arithmetic Spec ℤ × Spec ℤ producing the sign (RG-5, “the missing row”)
concepts.plain: In the relative Gram dictionary every entry has an analogue except the one that proves the sign: a Riemann–Roch or Grothendieck–Riemann–Roch theorem on an arithmetic square.
concepts.label: Open
concepts.core: RG-5: RR/GRR on an arithmetic “Spec ℤ × Spec ℤ” producing the sign — the missing row of the TAA Lemma 142 dictionary (TAA Lemma 142). D9: arithmetic GRR test on the scaling-site square (TAA Lemma 140/TAA Lemma 141 candidate).
concepts.proved: TAA Lemma 142 Thm 1.1: Weil Gram on translates is Toeplitz (flow), POLE = rank-2 signature (1,1) = the curve U-part exactly; every entry zero-free (flow, U/Tate poles, Γ_ℝ, Λ(n)); G_rel ≤ 0 on all spans ⇔ RH (Weil, restatement). Unconditional sign only on windows ≤ log 3 (TAA Lemma 10) and arch-only a* (TAA Lemma 127), both ghost-blind.
concepts.tests: Ghost ⇒ n₊(G_rel) = 2 (TAA Lemma 142); DH-location ghost positive from L* = 3.45. The theorem must produce G_rel ≤ 0 for ζ on every span without using zeros.

concepts.name: Relative Gram matrix G_rel
concepts.plain: Take a test function, translate it, and form the matrix of pairings after removing the pole plane. RH ⇔ this matrix is positive (semi)definite for all choices.
concepts.label: Restatement
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 149: prime side to x = e^16, exact u-space ARCH; hats h = 0.025, all 316 spans 0.25–16: ζ λ_max(G_rel) < 0 everywhere (−2.31e−6, −5.13e−9, −4.90e−11, −2.78e−11, −6.45e−12 at L = 1, 4, 8, 12, 16), n₊(C) = 1; roundoff floor 5e−15 (not a certificate).
pitfalls: Using the zero side to "check" it is tautological.
Negative sign is predicted both by RH and by any ghost with δ below the detection threshold (δ ≈ 0.01 at γ 85.7 by L = 16).

rels.note: [tested-by] DH prime side positive from L = 3.85 (TAA Lemma 149)

concepts.name: Verschiebung as the positive adjoint of Frobenius (F† = V)
concepts.plain: Frobenius has a partner map going the other way, Verschiebung, with F·V = q; the true statement behind RH is that V is the mirror image (adjoint) of F for a positive inner product, and J. W. McGreevy’s animation runs this pairing continuously.
concepts.label: Restatement
concepts.core: [T] On an elliptic curve over F_q: FV = VF = q and F + V = a (trace); deg(m − nF) = (m − nF)(m − nV) = m² − a·mn + q·n² (the norm conic); a² < 4q ⇒ ellipse and V = F̄ (complex conjugate eigenvalues), so |α|² = αᾱ = FV = q: Hasse; a² = 4q double line; a² > 4q hyperbola, F, V two different real numbers (a fake). Dieudonné modules W(k){F,V}/(FV − p); Rosati: π∘π† = q ⇒ π† = qπ⁻¹ = V (TAA Lemma 115 §6.1, Milne AV Lemma 1.2 as cited there). [R] The ghost-sensitive statement is V = F† for a POSITIVE form (Rosati trace form): ⟨Fx,Fy⟩ = q⟨x,y⟩ (Krein one-liner, definite_cup_square); for a finite model RH ⇔ there is a positive involution with F† = V (TAA Lemma 115 §6.3, via TAA Lemma 113 Thm 2.1). Flow form: adjoint = inverse up to eᵗ ⇔ Re ρ = ½. On the Eisenstein constant term Ve = Fr̄ on y^s iff Re s = ½ (TAA Lemma 115; a Ramanujan statement for E(·,s), not RH for ζ). [Ghost-blind] FV = q alone is pure algebra: any fake with char. poly x² − ax + q has V = a − F with FV = q (TAA Lemma 113 Thm 5.1 via TAA Lemma 115). concepts.name: Cayley–Klein absolute: definite ⇔ no real null rays (rotations vs boosts)
concepts.plain: A geometry is definite exactly when its absolute (the conic at infinity) has no real points; real points give boosts and null directions, i.e. ghosts.

Gap restated: is the absolute of the arithmetic pairing imaginary? Over F_q yes (Hodge index); for ζ this is MP4 ⇔ RH. J. W. McGreevy's withdrawn 45° null rays are the picture of the failure mode.

concepts.name: Limiting mixed Hodge structure / nilpotent and SL₂-orbit theorems (Schmid; CKS)

concepts.plain: Zeros on the line carry a sign; two can only leave the line together if they meet with opposite signs.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 111: semisimple unit-spectrum F strongly stable ⇔ Krein form definite on each eigenspace; ghosts born only at opposite-sign collisions (710/710 births). For ζ the graphical Krein sign alternates ⇒ no protection; Λ ≥ 0 ⇒ ζ not heat-flow stable.
pitfalls: Krein = stability, not positivity; presupposes unit spectrum (TAA Lemma 111 circularity).

concepts.name: RH for curves over F_q (Weil)
concepts.plain: For a curve over a finite field the Frobenius eigenvalues all have size √q. This is the one setting where TAA’s positivity is a theorem.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: Weil 1948: Castelnuovo–Severi / Hodge index on C×C ⇒ |α_i| = √q. Proved without the zeros: surface + ample class + Riemann–Roch ⇒ Hodge index ⇒ sign.
pitfalls: Weil already did column 2 (1940 note, 1948 books); the open step is column 3.

concepts.name: Ghost quartet ½ ± δ ± iγ
concepts.plain: A fake set of four zeros off the line, replacing a pair ½ ± iγ, used to test whether a criterion can detect RH failure.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 103 convention: replace ½ ± iγ by ½ ± δ ± iγ; each quartet gives 2 negative Weil eigenvalues; onsets L* listed.
pitfalls: δ convention conflict: δ = β − ½ (TAA Lemma 25/TAA Lemma 103/TAA Lemma 143) vs δ_ρ = 2β − 1 (TAA Lemma 144).

concepts.name: Decay rate ¼
concepts.plain: Every scattering resonance of the modular surface decays at rate ¼ exactly when its ζ-zero is on the line; an off-line zero decays at (1−β)/2 instead.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 118 Thm 3.1: ‖Z″‖ ≤ 1 unconditionally, poles at ρ/2 symmetric about ¼, rate (1−β)/2; RH ⇔ all rates ¼ [R]. TAA Lemma 120: spectral rate ¼, not uniform. TAA Lemma 143 SC-A (L + unitarity ⇒ κ ≡ ¼) ⇔ RH; ringing rate 0.24996 vs predicted ¼. TAA Lemma 144: μ = ¼ for every ρ (FE), ghost and DH ring at 0.0957414 = (1−β)/2.
concepts.formula: rate = (1 − β)/2; RH ⇔ all rates = ¼
pitfalls: The circular line for the modular surface is Re s = ¼, not ½ (TAA Lemma 143 corrections); rate = (1−β)/2, not Re ρ/2 (TAA Lemma 143 corrections).
No essential spectral gap for the modular surface (Bourgain–Dyatlov 1612.09040).

concepts.name: Eisenstein scattering resonances at s = ρ/2: purity at Re s = ¼
concepts.plain: At the cusp the Eisenstein series scatters with a phase of modulus one; its poles sit at half the zeta zeros, all on one line exactly when RH holds.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: φ(s) = ξ(2s−1)/ξ(2s) for SL₂(ℤ): |φ(½+it)| = 1 (NUM 2e−31), φ(s)φ(1−s) = 1 (FE, ghost-blind; NUM 8e−32). Zeros ρ of ζ give poles of φ at s = ρ/2 (simple: |φ|·ε → 0.5146 at ρ₁/2): under RH all on Re s = ¼ (one stratum); an off-line zero β + iγ would sit at Re s = β/2 (DH-type fake: 0.404, 0.0957, 0.325, 0.175 vs 0.25). Constant term a₀(y) = y^s + φ(s)y^{1−s} on s = ½+it: half-density lobes y^{½}e^{±it log y}. Where Selberg's zeta picks these up (Hejhal, Venkov): BIB, unopened.

concepts.name: Fake Weil polynomials (finite ghosts)
concepts.plain: Polynomials that look like curve zeta numerators (functional equation, integer counts) but have roots off the circle. They are the F_q test ghosts.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Fakes pass FE, count positivity, mod-2 data and the Hecke lattice (1,2); they fail Hodge index on ⟨H,V,Δ,Γ_{Fⁿ}⟩ (n₊ ≥ 2) and Rosati. Mixed fake (T² − 6T + 7)(T² + 7) passes N ≤ 2, fails from N = 4 (TAA Lemma 137, TAA Lemma 141).
pitfalls: Degenerate fakes (|α| ∈ {1, q}) cause pole-degenerate exceptions (TAA Lemma 92 C9).

concepts.name: Ghost map Δ_w: zeros right of σ from damped Dirichlet sums
concepts.plain: Subtract the smoothed comb from a damped prime sum: whatever is left is a bump at each zero that lies right of the observation line, and its phase tells how far right.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: [T] D_w(s) = Σ c(n) n^{−s} e^{−w² log² n/2} (entire), A_w = Gaussian-smoothed archimedean part, k_w*F_σ = smoothed comb on Re s = σ. Then A_w − D_w = Σ_ρ J_w(s−ρ) and Δ_w := A_w − D_w − k_w*F_σ = Σ_{β>σ} (√2π/w) exp((s−ρ)²/2w²): one Gaussian bump (width w) per zero right of σ, peak (√2π/w)e^{(β−σ)²/2w²}, phase slope (σ−β)/w² ⇒ γ̂, β̂, Γ̂ = 2(β̂−½). Identity holds whatever the zeros do (no RH content). Inputs: coefficients + Γ-factor + FE (F_σ by theta-function AFE); no zero list (TAA Lemma 155, correction 1). [N] DH: SNR (vs ζ control) ≥ 10 at X ≈ e^4 ≈ 55 (w = 0.4–0.5), β to 0.01 at X ≈ e^5 (w = 0.5, σ = 0.55), β̂ = 0.80852 / 0.65083 to ≤ 4e−9 at X = e^16 (SNR 6e6); ζ: no bump, floor ≤ 1e−6.
numbers: [N] AFE comb = TAA Lemma 154 direct to 6.5e−13 (DH, σ = 0.55), N = 13 terms suffice
[N] ghost map SNR ≥ 10 at log X = 4 (w ≥ 0.4)
pitfalls: Not coefficients alone: needs Γ-factor and FE inside the strip (TAA Lemma 155, correction 1).
Threshold measured only at t ≈ 86–114 (TAA Lemma 155, correction 7).
ζ null result proves nothing about RH.

concepts.name: Arithmetic unitarity ("RH = unitarity")
concepts.plain: TAA’s founding claim made precise: the scaling flow is always an isometry of the Weil form; RH is the statement that this form is positive, so the flow is genuinely unitary.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 1 Thm 2.1: (ii) T_t is a 𝒬-isometry unconditionally; (iii) growth exponent = Θ − ½; (iv) RH ⇔ 𝒬 ≥ 0 ⇔ unitary Hilbert realization ⇔ bounded matrix coefficients.
pitfalls: Isometry is free (Ax3-like); positivity of the form is the content (Ax2).

concepts.name: Goldfeld’s theorem (Euler product at s = 1 ⇒ RH, analytic order)
concepts.plain: If the partial Euler product of L(E,s) at the centre behaves like C/(log x)^r, then L(E,s) satisfies RH and r is the analytic order of vanishing — with a surprising √2 in the constant.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: If ∏_{p≤x} L_p(E,1) ∼ C/(log x)^r then L(E,s) satisfies RH, r = ord_{s=1}L(E,s), C = L^{(r)}(E,1)/(r! √2 e^{rγ}) (Goldfeld 1982, cited via Conrad 2005; TAA Lemma 140).
pitfalls: It gives the analytic order, not the rank (rank = order is BSD).
a_p are not BSD generators.
Note the √2 factor (Conrad).
Finite products (±10% oscillation to 1e7) are not evidence for RH (TAA Lemma 150, correction 10).

concepts.name: Epstein zeta no-go
concepts.plain: Epstein zeta functions of binary quadratic forms have a functional equation but no Euler product, and they have zeros off the line — the classic counterexample class next to DH.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 83: Epstein x² + 5y² = ζL(χ₋₂₀) + L(χ₋₄)L(χ₅); N(200) = 253 zeros, 183 on the line (70 off-line); first off-line 0.93297 + 15.66825i. TAA Lemma 135: 46 zeros with ½ < σ < 1 for t ≤ 250; control x² + y² (= 4ζL(χ₋₄), has Euler product): 0. TAA Lemma 138 R4: theta inversion and FE hold, unitarity ⇒ FE only, ghost-blind (Thm). TAA Lemma 153 (G, CM points): Σ′(m²+n²)^{−s} = 4ζ(s)L(s,χ₋₄) (NUM s = 3: 4.6589136156); Σ′(m²+mn+n²)^{−s} = 6ζ(s)L(s,χ₋₃) (6.3758815528); x²+5y²: ζ_K + L(χ₋₄)L(χ₅), 2x²+2xy+3y²: ζ_K − L(χ₋₄)L(χ₅), sum over the class group = 2ζ_K (Euler product restored, Hecke; NUM to 1e−12). Off-line zero refined: 0.9329696975 + 15.6682495313i (|Z| = 3e−21; ζ_K there 0.933). CM points are where one restricts (toric periods), not a quotient (TAA Lemma 153, correction 22).

concepts.name: Compatible complex structure J commuting with Frobenius
concepts.plain: A quarter-turn that commutes with Frobenius and makes the form positive; it exists exactly when the curve satisfies RH.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: J = (2F − a)/√(4q − a²) (TAA Lemma 101) exists only if a² < 4q; 2^g sign choices, exactly one positive. Finite: compatible J with [J,F] = 0 ⇔ F unitary semisimple (TAA Lemma 104). For ζ: J exists ⇔ RH (restatement, TAA Lemma 104 dichotomy).
numbers: g = 1, q = 101: J = J_F exact; ghosts give Cl(1,1)
pitfalls: A quartet J is symplectic but never compatible (sig (2,2)) (TAA Lemma 110).
With a W-independent form J is unconditional but ghost-blind (TAA Lemma 104).

concepts.name: de Branges spaces
concepts.plain: Hilbert spaces of entire functions built from a Hermite–Biehler function E; RH becomes "E_h is Hermite–Biehler", but de Branges’ stronger positivity conditions are known to fail for ζ.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 36 Thm 3.1: for h ∈ (0,½], all β ≤ ½ + h ⇔ PR on σ > ½ + h ⇔ E_{h′} HB ∀h′ > h; h = ½ free, h → 0 = RH. Conrey–Li 2000 (opened, TAA Lemma 78): de Branges positivity fails for ζ and χ₄. TAA Lemma 118: Ψ_c passive ⇔ E_c = ξ(·+c) Hermite–Biehler. TAA Lemma 34: Suzuki’s de Branges line from the prime side.
pitfalls: Conrey–Li: de Branges’ stronger conditions fail — beware "positivity ⇒ RH" shortcuts.

concepts.name: de Bruijn–Newman constant Λ
concepts.plain: Heat flow on ξ; Λ ≥ 0 (Rodgers–Tao), RH ⇔ Λ = 0.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: Λ ≥ 0 ⇒ ζ not heat-flow stable (TAA Lemma 111). Healing times TAA Lemma 124/TAA Lemma 136 conflict. TAA Lemma 150 (opened): Rodgers–Tao Λ ≥ 0 (Forum Math Pi 2020), Polymath 15 Λ ≤ 0.22; H_0(z) = Ξ(z/2)/8, so t_RT = 4·t_Ξ (TAA Lemma 150, correction 8). DH heuristic (truncated list): pair at 85.70 closes at t_RT ≈ 0.177 (isolated 2δ² = 0.190); does not separate DH from ζ's known range.
pitfalls: t* = 2δ² vs δ²/2.

concepts.name: Hasse bound as a positive degree form
aliases: Q_p = x² + a_p xy + p y²
concepts.plain: For an elliptic curve the degree of an endomorphism is a positive quadratic form; Hasse’s bound is that this form is positive (Cauchy–Schwarz / Pythagoras).
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: deg(m + nπ) = m² + amn + qn² is PD ⇔ a² < 4q; Hasse = Cauchy–Schwarz. Ghost a = 25, q = 101: deg(10 − π) = −49 (TAA Lemma 106).
concepts.formula: m² + a mn + q n² > 0 ⇔ a² < 4q

concepts.name: Li criterion
concepts.plain: RH ⇔ the Li coefficients are non-negative.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: Li 1997 / Bombieri–Lagarias 1999: RH ⇔ λ_n ≥ 0 for all n — the Weil positivity in another basis. TAA Lemma 112 reads the Weil form as a Toeplitz–Carathéodory problem; TAA Lemma 131: no route supplies the positivity.

concepts.name: Suzuki’s de Branges line from the prime side
concepts.plain: A de Branges / transmission-line object built from prime data whose passivity along the whole line is equivalent to RH.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: Su21 (Suzuki JFA 281 (2021) 109116): E^{ω,ν} = ξ(½ + ω − iz)^ν, νω > 1, Hankel kernel from prime-side data (TAA Lemma 34). TAA Lemma 37: headline exponential line Θ_c = exp(−2c ξ′/ξ); ‖𝒦[t]‖ < 1 ∀t ⇔ sup ≤ 1; weak form sup_t ≤ 1 ⇔ RH; "sup < 1" is false in the passive case; strict pointwise bound open (M11).
pitfalls: "sup < 1" is false in the passive case; the correct form is sup ≤ 1 (TAA Lemma 37).

concepts.name: Bagchi recurrence
concepts.plain: RH ⇔ ζ approximates itself in the strip (strong recurrence).
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: Bagchi (via Nakamura Thm B): RH ⇔ strong recurrence of ζ for all K, ε ("infinite prime bath still recurs", TAA Lemma 118). TAA Lemma 123 local form [T given Voronin + Carlson]: ζ strongly recurrent on a disc K ⇔ no zero on K; ghosts show up as a local Rouché defect. Finite prime baths recur but are ghost-blind.

concepts.name: Gain lines (active media)
concepts.plain: A ghost acts like a gain line: negative absorption.
concepts.label: Analogy
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 146 §2: Re ξ′/ξ = Σ(σ−β)/((σ−β)² + (t−γ)²) — each zero is an absorption line to its right; an off-line zero gives a gain line. Grid σ ∈ [.505,1.1], t ∈ [80,92]: ξ min +0.00467; DH −66.84 at (0.794, 85.70), 1.89% negative; TAA Lemma 144 ghost −66.97 (1.94%). Lorentz model: dRe χ/dω −6 (absorber) / +6 (gain). TAA Lemma 154: measured widths — the near line of a DH ghost on σ = ½+d has FWHM 2|d − (β−½)| (match ≤ 3e−6, 13 d), inverted for d < β−½; as d → 0 its FWHM → Γ = 2(β−½) from below; the visible feature (near − mirror) keeps width ≈ ½(β−½) while its depth fades as 2d/(β−½)². KK sign invariant κ = Re F·∂_tIm F = −1/a³ flips at a gain line. [N] TAA Lemma 155: DH's gain lines reconstructed from ≈ 10 nonzero coefficients via the theta AFE (N = 13), and detected as ghost-map bumps from damped Dirichlet sums with X ≈ 55.

concepts.name: Near-null direction of ζ's relative Gram matrix
concepts.plain: The direction where ζ's relative Gram matrix is closest to zero is a function whose Fourier transform lives almost entirely below the first zero γ₁.
concepts.label: Numerical

concepts.name: Integer dimension over 𝕊 (minimal generators)
concepts.plain: On Spec ℤ̄ Connes–Consani’s dimension is an integer: the least number of generators over the sphere spectrum. The log-theta dimension of van der Geer–Schoof is a different, "virtual" count that agrees up to a bounded error.
concepts.label: Numerical
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 147 [N]: brute force dim_𝕊(HZ)_[−m,m] = n + 1 for all m ≤ 16; dim_𝕊[±1] = ⌈log₃(2n+1)⌉ for all n ≤ 40; dim_𝕊 − vdGS h⁰/log 2 ∈ [1.016, 1.983]. TAA Lemma 147, correction 1: Dim_ℝ on C_p is a covering dimension, not a theta count.
pitfalls: Do not identify CC dimension with theta/lattice counts (TAA Lemma 147, correction 1).

concepts.name: Hodge index theorem
concepts.plain: On a surface the intersection form has exactly one positive direction (the ample class); everything orthogonal to it is negative. This sign is what proves RH for curves.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: NS(C×C) ⊗ ℝ has signature (1, ρ−1); U = ⟨f₁,f₂⟩ is the (1,1) part and its complement is negative definite. Over ℚ, Hodge-index form on V₀ ⇔ RH (TAA Lemma 91, restatement). Surface + ample + RR ⇒ Hodge index (D8).
concepts.formula: sig NS = (1, ρ − 1); D·D ≤ 0 on h^⊥
pitfalls: Effectivity and Hodge index are independent on both sides (TAA Lemma 94).
Hodge index needs S2, S3, S5 too (TAA Lemma 145).

concepts.name: Osterwalder–Schrader reflection positivity
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 25 Prop 6.3: OS-RP for Weil with θu = −u FAILS (atom δ_{log2}: RP ≍ −1/ε, −2.50, −11.08, −35.58, −121.35 at ε = 0.1…0.003); OS gives H ≥ 0 semigroup, Weil a unitary group. TAA Lemma 32: RH ⇔ |OS_a| ≤ Q on E₊(a) (domination form); OS-RP false unconditionally. TAA Lemma 42 Thm 2.1/2.2/4.4 (Hankel ≠ Toeplitz; orthogonality pincer). TAA Lemma 47: reflection ⇒ FE, positivity needs polarization. Closest literature: Neeb–Ólafsson RP ↔ Lax–Phillips. TAA Lemma 151: failure at log 2 = smallest prime, not wildness; half density = the reflection (unitary) half of OS. TAA Lemma 153 (claim 6): for Gaussian data RP ⇔ the reflected form B(f,g) = ⟨θf,g⟩ is PSD on the positive-time space ⇔ every 2-plane restriction is an ellipse or degenerate (trivially, since 1-dim restrictions suffice); NOT ⇔ 'the blocks of one chosen decomposition are ellipses' unless they are B-orthogonal (TAA Lemma 153, correction 6). TAA Lemma 153's R-symmetric tilt blocks are reflection pairs (f₊, f₋ = Rf₊).

concepts.name: Legendre strata: support function / Fenchel–Moreau as a definiteness detector
concepts.plain: All the information about a convex curve sits in the intercepts of its tangent lines; the Legendre transform returns the curve exactly when it is convex, so it is a definiteness test.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Tangent lines carry a convex curve: the support function h(θ) = sup_{x∈K}⟨x,u_θ⟩ determines a closed convex K (Minkowski; BIB). For f = ½xᵀAx the Legendre transform is ½pᵀA⁻¹p, finite everywhere iff A ≻ 0; if A has a negative eigenvalue f* ≡ +∞ (on a box |x| ≤ R it grows with R: TAA Lemma 153 NUM). Fenchel–Moreau: f** = f iff f is convex lsc (BIB). Support-function window of a conic region: 2π for an ellipse; for one convex hyperbola branch exactly 2·atan√(|λ₋|/λ₊) < π (NUM 64.8° vs 64.62° predicted for λ = 1, −0.4); for both branches (or the region xᵀAx ≤ 1 with A indefinite) empty; jump 2π → 0 at det = 0. J. W. McGreevy's 'Legendre type concept' is this.

concepts.name: Hodge–Riemann bilinear relations
concepts.plain: Pairing a holomorphic form with its own complex conjugate gives a positive number: a genuine |amplitude|².
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: HR holds on every compact Riemann surface; HR form = 2 × Petersson (TAA Lemma 134). Positivity = complex structure inserted (Weil operator C = i^{p−q}). Hecke self-adjointness gives a_p ∈ ℝ, not |a_p| ≤ 2√p.
pitfalls: Column 2 (F_q) never fully inherited the HR sign; Castelnuovo replaces it algebraically (TAA Lemma 140).

concepts.name: Lax–Phillips scattering
concepts.plain: Scattering theory for waves on the modular surface; resonances relate to zeros.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: LP80 (read at source, TAA Lemma 118/TAA Lemma 141): s(z) = Λ(2s−1)/Λ(2s), Res_{s=1} = 3/π, poles at zeros of ζ(1+2iz), RH ⇒ Im z = ¼; Pavlov–Faddeev "RH iff Z″ decays exponentially"; spectrum of B″ = {(κ−1)/2}; "all that is missing is an appropriate inner product". TAA Lemma 118 Thm 3.1: ‖Z″‖ ≤ 1 unconditionally. TAA Lemma 153: bib verified by Crossref: Lax–Phillips, Scattering Theory for Automorphic Functions, Ann. Math. Stud. 87 (Princeton 1976; De Gruyter record dated 1977), doi 10.1515/9781400881567; Bull. AMS 2 (1980) 261–295 (Crossref pages; TAA Lemma 141 cited 261–296, TAA Lemma 153, correction 31); Pavlov–Faddeev, J. Soviet Math. 3 (1975) 522–548, doi 10.1007/BF01084688 (Zap. LOMI 27 (1972)). concepts.name: Laguerre's formula: angle = (1/2i) log cross-ratio with the circular points
concepts.plain: The angle between two lines is read off at infinity, from how the lines sit relative to two imaginary points; the metric lives at infinity.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: θ(ℓ₁,ℓ₂) = (1/2i) log CR(ℓ₁,ℓ₂; I, J), I, J = (1 : ±i : 0), isotropic lines y = ±ix; CR = (m₁−i)(m₂+i)/((m₁+i)(m₂−i)) = e^{2i(θ₁−θ₂)} (TAA Lemma 152 NUM 7.1e−16, 2000 pairs). The ½: θ is defined mod π (ℝP¹). The Euclidean metric is the pair {I, J} at infinity (the absolute). Resolves J. W. McGreevy's paradox: lines through 0 are not parallel at infinity (Riemann sphere: they meet again at ∞ with the same angle, opposite orientation; ℝP²: distinct points at infinity); the angle at 0 becomes a separation at infinity.
pitfalls: Sign/orientation conventions: with CR as written Laguerre gives θ₁ − θ₂ mod π; only |θ| mod π is canonical (TAA Lemma 152, correction 9).
Laguerre 1853 (Nouv. Ann. 12, 57–66): Numdam record and first page opened; the formula’s place in the paper not seen.

concepts.name: Connes–Consani sites
concepts.plain: Topos-theoretic candidate for Spec ℤ × Spec ℤ.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: Arithmetic site and scaling site (CC14, CC16): a square exists, with Ψ_λ and s(f,f) = D•D (TAA Lemma 30), but no H¹, RR or Hodge index on it (TAA Lemma 65). TAA Lemma 147: their proved RRs are 1-dimensional; RR on the square is open (CC18).

concepts.name: Deligne's route: Lefschetz pencils, monodromy and Rankin's tensor-power trick
concepts.plain: Deligne proved the Weil conjectures without the Hodge index theorem, but still with a positivity: Rankin’s positivity of coefficients of tensor powers.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: Deligne, Weil I (Publ. IHÉS 43, 1974, 273–307): RH over F_q without a Hodge index theorem — Lefschetz pencils and monodromy (SGA 7) reduce to a local system on a curve; Rankin's trick (Rankin 1939) bounds weights through L-functions of tensor powers. It still uses positivity: of the coefficients of those L-functions (TAA Lemma 152, correction 4). For ζ no tensor-power analogue is known to give more than zero-free regions (Heuristic, BR-4).
concepts.uncertain: Numdam record and reference list opened; the argument itself is standard knowledge (BIB), not re-read.
pitfalls: 'No positivity' is wrong: Rankin's coefficient positivity is used; what is avoided is a Hodge index theorem (TAA Lemma 152, correction 4).

concepts.name: Selberg eigenvalue conjecture ↔ mass shell λ = ¼ + r²
concepts.plain: The Laplacian on the modular surface is positive, which forces its eigenvalues onto a line; whether the first eigenvalue is at least ¼ for all congruence groups is still open.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: Δ ≥ 0 on L²(Γ∖ℍ), λ = s(1−s) real ⇒ s ∈ [0,1] or Re s = ½; for SL₂(ℤ) λ₁ = ¼ + 9.53369…² ≈ 91.14 > ¼, so the spectral zeros of Selberg's zeta (cusp forms) lie on Re s = ½. Selberg's conjecture λ₁ ≥ ¼ for congruence subgroups: open; Selberg 3/16 (1965), Kim–Sarnak 975/4096 = ¼ − (7/64)² ≈ 0.2380 (appendix to Kim, JAMS 16 (2003) 139–183; bib data Crossref, bound via secondary sources). Shape analogy: ρ(1−ρ) = ¼ + γ² ≥ ¼ real ⇔ ρ on the line (or real) (Analogy).

concepts.name: Cartan involution / compact unitary group
concepts.plain: A positive involution is the same thing as a compact (rotation-type) symmetry group; Albert lists the possible kinds.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Positive involution ⇔ compact unitary group (TAA Lemma 99, Milne Prop 1.20); Rosati = Cartan θ_J on commutant of J; Weil numbers generate CM or totally real fields (TAA Lemma 136); Albert types I–IV.
pitfalls: Abelian scaling has only an outer Cartan U(1); zeros-as-angles = RH (circular, TAA Lemma 99).

rels.note: no compact Hodge circle for ℚ (TAA Lemma 100)

concepts.name: Maxwell construction / convex effective potential
aliases: convex hull of a double well
concepts.plain: Doing the Legendre transform twice fills in a double well with a flat floor; this convexity comes for free only from a positive measure.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: The effective potential Γ = (log Z)* is convex automatically (a Legendre transform); for a double well the biconjugate V** is the convex envelope, flat between the two minima (Maxwell's common tangent; TAA Lemma 153 figure). log ∫e^{Jφ}dμ is convex in J by Hölder when μ ≥ 0; for a signed μ it can fail (TAA Lemma 153 example μ = ½δ₋₁ − 0.6δ₀ + ½δ₁). Physics citation left uncited (none opened).
pitfalls: No physics source opened; Hölder argument proved inline (TAA Lemma 153 §2).

rels.note: convexity needs a positive measure: Weil’s form has signed prime terms

concepts.name: Pole plane / Tate poles at s = 0, 1
concepts.plain: The two poles of ξ(s) at s = 0 and 1 give the reference plane; subtracting them is what makes a form "relative".
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 142: the relative Gram on translates uses the pole terms f̂(0), f̂(1) (zero-free entries). Pole of ζ at s = 1 is the 𝕃-ray; the functional equation pairs it with s = 0.

concepts.name: Products grow linearly (2n), not quadratically
concepts.plain: Sections on naive products of Spec ℤ̄ grow only linearly in n (slope 2); a genuine surface needs quadratic growth, which forces the rank to grow with n.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 147 [T/N]: product sandwich ⌈log₂ #⌉ ≤ dim_𝕊(box) ≤ Σ dims, exact = additive bound in 6/6 boxes; fixed rank ⇒ linear: Spec ℤ̄² fits 1.99993n + 2.0009 (vs 2n + 4); quadratic growth ⇒ rank ≳ n. Same as TAA Lemma 145 Thm linear (fixed-rank lattice ⇒ h⁰ linear, h⁰/n = 2.000 at n = 400).

concepts.name: Weight–monodromy conjecture (Deligne): status
concepts.plain: Deligne conjectured that the monodromy filtration and Frobenius weights match; it is proved in characteristic p and in many but not all mixed-characteristic cases.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: For X proper smooth over a local field, Frobenius weights on gr_j^N H^i are i + j. Proved: equal characteristic (Deligne, Weil II 1980, over a curve; general char p via Terasoma, Ito); dim ≤ 2 in mixed characteristic (Rapoport–Zink + de Jong); p-adically uniformized varieties (Ito; Dat); cases of Shimura varieties; set-theoretic complete intersections in projective smooth toric varieties (Scholze, Publ. IHÉS 116, 2012, Thm 1.14). Open in general in mixed characteristic. (Curves and abelian varieties: curves are in dim ≤ 2; abelian varieties BIB, not opened.)

concepts.name: Yoneda specification
concepts.plain: Specify the object by its properties (Ax1–Ax3).
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 90: bare Hom sets do not determine an object (ℚ vs ℚ^(N)); naturality needed; representability ⇒ uniqueness/functoriality, presupposes positivity if it is an axiom. TAA Lemma 98 Prop 6.1: representable ⇒ unique; 𝔉(pt) ≠ ∅ ⇒ RH; "representability is the whole battle" (TAA Lemma 98, correction 19). TAA Lemma 137: T_W with Ax1–Ax3; existence open.

concepts.name: Organizing split: ghost-blind = phase, ghost-sensitive = sign
concepts.plain: Every test that ghosts pass is about phase/unitarity; every test that catches a ghost is about the sign of a spectral weight, and for ζ that sign is RH.
concepts.label: Heuristic
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 146 synthesis: functional equation, |φ| = 1, cocycles, Hecke, cusp positivity are ghost-blind (Ax3); Lagarias sign, Weil sign, Rosati sign are ghost-sensitive (Ax2) and ⇔ RH for ζ. Every ghost-sensitive global quadratic statement for Spec ℤ found so far is a restatement.
numbers: DH: FE to 5×10⁻¹⁵ yet Re ξ′/ξ = −66.8
pitfalls: An organizing observation, not a theorem: "sign" items for curves are theorems, for ζ restatements.

concepts.name: Must-fail-for-DH acceptance test
concepts.plain: Any future Riemann–Roch on the square must be false for Davenport–Heilbronn; otherwise it cannot prove RH. So it has to use the Euler product.
concepts.label: Heuristic
concepts.core: All H⁰-side objects are built from ℤ ⊂ 𝔸_ℚ and are ghost-blind; the topological side s(f,f) is ghost-sensitive (TAA Lemma 142: DH-location ghost positive from L* = 3.45, actual DH from 4.70). Hence an RR theorem on the square must FAIL for DH ⇒ must use the Euler product / ring structure (necessary condition, proposed acceptance test, TAA Lemma 147).
concepts.uncertain: Proposed acceptance test.
pitfalls: A necessary condition only.

rels.note: proved RRs pass DH, so cannot decide RH

concepts.name: BRST / Gupta–Bleuler physical quotient
concepts.plain: Remove null and negative-norm states to get a positive physical space — as U^⊥ in Hodge index.
concepts.label: Analogy
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 115: BRST structure exact over F_q and ℚ [T]; "no ghosts" ⇔ RH [R]; missing positive V ≅ H¹ (Hilbert–Pólya) ⇒ restatement. Kugo–Ojima (TAA Lemma 146 §1, Analogy): BRST quartets are the closest physics analogue of ζ’s zero quartets, but a BRST quartet DECOUPLES (its ker Q part is null and is quotiented out), while a ghost quartet SURVIVES in the relative quotient with two positive directions (TAA Lemma 142). Higgs/ghost cancellation: which modes are physical vs null = the ghost question; Analogy only.
concepts.uncertain: PM-3 open.
pitfalls: PM-3 is open.

concepts.name: Γ, the width of a zero: FWHM of its Breit–Wigner line
concepts.plain: Each zero shows up as a bell-shaped line; its width at the critical line is twice its distance from the line. RH says every width is zero: every line becomes a spike.
concepts.label: Restatement
concepts.core: [T] On Re s = σ each zero ρ = β+iγ contributes to Re ξ′/ξ the signed line (σ−β)/((σ−β)²+(t−γ)²): FWHM 2|σ−β|, height 1/(σ−β), area π·sgn(σ−β) (Hadamard; TAA Lemma 146). [R] Γ_ρ := 2|β−½| = lim_{σ→½} FWHM (signed Γ± = 2(β−½); FE mirror has −Γ±); s = ½+iE puts ρ at E = γ − iΓ±/2. RH ⇔ all Γ_ρ = 0 ⇔ every line sharpens to πδ_γ as σ↓½. Γ is a limit, not observable on σ = ½ itself (Re ξ′/ξ ≡ 0 there by the FE; TAA Lemma 154, correction 6). 'Stable vs decaying' is convention-dependent; invariant: unitary state vs non-unitary ±Γ pair (in u = log x the ghost grows like e^{Γu/2}; TAA Lemma 154, correction 3). [N] TAA Lemma 154: ζ (5 zeros) and DH on-line: measured FWHM = 2d to 3.3e−7 rel over 13 lines d ∈ [0.01, 0.5], area π to 6e−7; DH ghosts: near line FWHM 2|d − (β−½)| (≤ 3e−6), flips to a gain line for d < β−½, → Γ = 0.617 / 0.302 from below (0.5970 / 0.2816 at d = 0.01; TAA Lemma 154, correction 2: not 'at least Γ'); visible feature width ≈ ½(β−½) constant, depth ≈ 2d/(β−½)² → 0; planted ghost (0.8, 40) identical. [N] TAA Lemma 155: Γ recovered without a zero list — Γ̂ = 2(β̂−½) = 0.61703, 0.30166 from the ghost map's phase slope (coefficients + Γ-factor + FE); exact comb from the theta AFE agrees with TAA Lemma 154 to 1e−12. Recorded in TAA Lemma 155 §0; certification in TAA Lemma 156. TAA Lemma 156 [N, rigorous]: certified (Arb) Γ₁ = 0.617034364913274771106 ± 9e−22, Γ₂ = 0.30166016121947416481 ± 3e−21; [T given certificates] flips at d* = β−½ in (0.30,0.35), (0.15,0.20); ζ targets simple on the line ⇒ FWHM 2d exact; ghost FWHM → Γ from below; [N] TAA Lemma 154 fits certified to first order (rel ≤ 1.6e−5; ghost 2 ≤ 6.3e−5 after tail subtraction).

concepts.name: Mass shell / even Ξ: s(1−s) = ¼ + t²
concepts.plain: Rewrite the zeros as 'masses squared': RH says every one of them is a real number at least ¼, like a stable particle.
concepts.label: Restatement
concepts.core: Ξ(t) = ξ(½+it) even and real ⇒ Ξ(t) = F(t²); RH ⇔ every root z = t² of F is real and positive ⇔ every nontrivial ρ(1−ρ) = σ(1−σ) + t² + it(1−2σ) is real and ≥ ¼ (then ρ(1−ρ) = ¼ + z). Dictionary: mass² = ¼ = ρ² (half density), momentum t; off-line pair = complex mass² (DH: z₀ = 7344.283 − 52.879i); real zero in (0,1) = tachyon. Connes 1999: 'positivity properties of Δ = D(1−D)', Selberg Laplacian λ = s(1−s) ≥ ¼.

concepts.name: Why the area is π: the circle in every zero count (Basel as common origin)
concepts.plain: The π in each zero’s area is the circle’s π, coming from the geometry of complex numbers; the same circle gives Euler’s π²/6, but the zeros do not explain π.
concepts.label: Restatement
concepts.core: [T] ∫ a/(a²+x²)dx = π sgn a = angle subtended by ℝ at ia = half of ∮dz/z = 2πi; P_a = (1/π)a/(a²+x²) is harmonic measure, Cayley-equivalent to the disk Poisson kernel (mass 1, NUM 40 digits); 2π = circumference/radius. [R] Area is a dimensionless invariant of the complex structure (scale- and coordinate-free yes), as C/d is of a round metric. Direction: the circle puts π into every zero count; the zeros do not derive π (TAA Lemma 154, correction 9). [T] Euler: ζ(2) = π²/6, ζ(2k) = rational·π^{2k} (sin product / π cot πz; NUM sanity ζ(2) − π²/6 = 2e−41). [R] Basel and the ±π area share an origin (the circle); NOT (±π)²/6 from residue areas: ζ(2k) is archimedean (Γ-factor, trivial zeros; ζ(1−2k) = −B_{2k}/2k) (TAA Lemma 154, correction 10). [C/O] ζ(3) irrational (Apéry, BIB); rationality of ζ(3)/π³ OPEN (TAA Lemma 154, correction 11); even/odd ↔ ghost-blind/sensitive is Heuristic at most. The locked ratio is the complex structure J, which also defines the Weil operator C = i^{p−q} (OS/Wick reading Analogy, TAA Lemma 153, correction 10).
pitfalls: Not a derivation of π from zeros or RH (TAA Lemma 154, correction 9).
ζ(2) is not a product of resonance areas (TAA Lemma 154, correction 10).
ζ(3)/π³ irrational is unproved (TAA Lemma 154, correction 11).

concepts.name: Two-point form g + iω ≥ 0
concepts.plain: Combine a metric g and symplectic ω into one Hermitian form; positivity ⇔ Weil.
concepts.label: Restatement
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 103: g + iω ≥ 0 ⇔ Weil ⇔ RH.

concepts.name: Riemann hypothesis (target node)
concepts.plain: All nontrivial zeros of ζ have real part ½. In TAA every ghost-sensitive global sign statement for Spec ℤ turns out to be RH restated.
concepts.label: Open
concepts.core: RH is not proved in TAA. The positivity inventory of the programme finds that every ghost-sensitive global quadratic statement for Spec ℤ is a restatement of RH.

pitfalls: Every lemma PDF carries "RH NOT proved".

concepts.name: Hilbert–Pólya
concepts.plain: Find a self-adjoint operator with spectrum the γ’s.
concepts.label: Open
concepts.core: Standard program: a self-adjoint/unitary realization with spectrum the γ’s would give RH. TAA verdicts: spinor route = Hilbert–Pólya in Clifford dress (TAA Lemma 104); 2B″ + ½ needs an inner product (TAA Lemma 105, LP80 "all that is missing is an appropriate inner product"); missing positive V ≅ H¹ (TAA Lemma 115); circular if the inner product is Weil’s form (TAA Lemma 138 R2); lossless Heaviside realization = Hilbert–Pólya [O] (TAA Lemma 144 HS-F). TAA Lemma 154: 'all widths Γ_ρ vanish' ⇔ RH ⇔ the γ's are the spectrum of some self-adjoint operator — content-free without a natural operator (TAA Lemma 154, correction 5).

concepts.name: Arithmetic Castelnuovo object (C1–C4)
concepts.plain: Requirements an arithmetic surface would need to reproduce the curve proof.
concepts.label: Open
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 136: an arithmetic Castelnuovo object needs (C1) infinite H¹, (C2) positive involution, (C3) u_t u_t† = e^t, (C4) positivity proved without zeros; circularity flagged (TAA Lemma 106). TAA Lemma 138: the Čech 2-class supplies C2–C3 structure but not the sign. TAA Lemma 147: the decisive missing objects are H¹ on the square, an NS ⊋ U containing Ψ_λ, and quadratic RR.

concepts.name: No Riemann–Roch for C_ℚ × C_ℚ (the square is open)

concepts.label: Open

TAA Lemma 147 (iv): decisive missing objects = H¹ on the square, an intersection theory putting Ψ_λ into an NS larger than U, and quadratic RR.
pitfalls: Do not cite a CC Riemann–Roch on the square: none exists (TAA Lemma 147, correction 2).

concepts.name: Time delay (Wigner)
concepts.plain: How long a wave packet lingers in the cusp; unlike the winding of the phase, the time-delay peak does see ghosts.
concepts.label: Analogy
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 143: winding ½ per zero for all β (ghost-blind), but time-delay peak at r = 42.85 is 3.09 (ζ), 27.22 (ζ + TAA Lemma 103 ghost), 27.42 (DH): ghost-sensitive. ζ time delay is negative for r ≲ 2.9 (min −3.87), so "positive delay" fails for ζ. TAA Lemma 120: dwell time ∂_x log|Φ| = −θ′(ω). TAA Lemma 118: Connes harmonic measure of an off-line zero = (1/2π) × TAA Lemma 117 excess group delay. TAA Lemma 153: Wigner time delay = −φ′/φ(½+it) = 2π dξ/dt (Birman–Krein); Wigner 1955 (Phys. Rev. 98, 145–147, doi 10.1103/PhysRev.98.145; Crossref) gives a causality lower bound, not positivity; ζ's delay negative only through −1/(¼+t²) (t ≤ 2.8); DH's positive everywhere, ghost = peak 27.27 at 42.84. TAA Lemma 154: the Wigner delay −φ′/φ is a sum of positive Breit–Wigner lines (two per zero, HWHM β/2, (1−β)/2); the group delay of ξ along σ (Re ξ′/ξ) is a sum of signed ones; negative group delay in Re s > ½ is a ghost (TAA Lemma 154, correction 12: optics 'superluminal is harmless' does not transfer).

concepts.plain: Physical theories have non-negative spectral weight; ζ analogue is the sign of zero weights.

concepts.name: Birman–Krein bridge: scattering phase = spectral shift; −φ′/φ = spectral density = Wigner delay = Maass–Selberg intercept
concepts.plain: The scattering phase at the cusp counts states; its derivative is a sum of positive bumps, one pair per zeta zero, whose widths tell where the zero sits.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Birman–Krein (Dokl. 144 (1962) 475–478): det S(λ) = e^{−2πiξ(λ)} [Cs]. Cusp of SL₂(ℤ): S = φ (one cusp), φ(½+it) = Λ(2it)/Λ(1+2it), |φ| = 1 (NUM 3.9e−31, t ≤ 60), so dξ/dt = (1/2π)(−φ′/φ)(½+it) (sign convention). THEOREM (Hadamard; NUM ≤ 3.9e−6 with 1517 zeros + tail): −φ′/φ(½+it) = −1/(¼+t²) + Σ_ρ [a/(a²+(t−γ/2)²) + b/(b²+(t−γ/2)²)], a = (1−β)/2, b = β/2: each zero gives two Lorentzians of mass π (winding ghost-blind), widths ghost-sensitive. The only negative term is the ζ pole term −1/(¼+t²) (negativity t ≤ 2.8; TAA Lemma 153, correction 23 refined). DH (Λ entire): −φ′/φ > 0 everywhere (min 0.41 on [0.5,60]) even with its ghost, so density positivity is ghost-blind (TAA Lemma 153, correction 29); ghost = narrow Lorentzians (peak 27.27 at t = 42.84; predicted ghost part 25.84). The ratio across the y-axis = φ; for ζ the analogous ratio is χ(s) = ζ(s)/ζ(1−s), χ(½+it) = e^{−2iθ(t)} gives the smooth part θ/π of N(T).

concepts.name: Ghost conventions (δ, heat-flow healing)

concepts.core: Unconditional: κ(𝒬) = N₊ (TAA Lemma 1 Thm 2.1); each ghost quartet gives 2 negative eigenvalues (TAA Lemma 103, Bombieri). Finite form: n₋ = k_r + 2k_c = ½ rk E² (TAA Lemma 110 Thm 2.3); Rosati n₋ = k = τ + ½Z_off = n₊(NS) − 1 (TAA Lemma 88 Thm B).

concepts.name: S(T) = (1/π) arg ζ(½+iT): the fluctuating remainder of N(T)
concepts.plain: The zero count is a smooth main term plus a wiggly remainder S(T); a fake zero off the line only shows up when the count is compared with the sign changes on the line.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: N(T) = θ(T)/π + 1 + S(T) (ζ); the smooth part is the phase winding of χ, S(T) the remainder. Ghost status (TAA Lemma 153, correction 28): S(T) and N(T) count ALL zeros in the strip (argument principle), so S(T) alone is ghost-blind; the ghost shows only against the on-line count N₀(T) (Hardy-Z sign changes): DH 62 sign changes vs N = 66 on [10,120], deficits exactly 2 in [80,90] and [110,120] (TAA Lemma 152). The cusp phase φ smooths S out: its zero information arrives as Lorentzians of width ≥ min(β,1−β)/2.

concepts.name: Two partners of a zero (duality vs conjugation)
concepts.plain: Every zero has a duality partner (from the functional equation) and a conjugate partner; RH says the two coincide.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 93 Thm 1.1: duality partner (Poincaré duality/cup product, ghosts too) and conjugation partner; RH ⇔ partners coincide. Rosati Tr(p(F)p(F)†) and the Weil zero side have the same "zero × duality partner" shape.

concepts.name: Connes–Consani Riemann–Roch on Spec ℤ̄ (1-dimensional)
concepts.plain: Connes and Consani proved Riemann–Roch for the compactified Spec ℤ, counting sections by integer numbers of generators; it is a one-dimensional "χ = degree + constant" law and cannot see D².
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: CC23 Thm 1.1/5.1 over 𝕊: dim H⁰ − dim H¹ = ⌈deg₂D⌉′ + 1 (genus 0, base 2, no exceptional set); CC22 over 𝕊[±1]: ⌈(deg D + log 2)/log 3⌉′ − 1_L, duality H⁰(K−D) ≅ Hom(H¹(D), U(1)_{1/4}), K = −2{2}; scaling site Thm 5.17 Dim_ℝ H⁰(D) − Dim_ℝ H⁰(−D) = deg D. Verdict (TAA Lemma 147): all proved RRs are 1-dimensional, χ = deg + const ⇒ blind to D² by TAA Lemma 145 parity.

Dim_ℝ is a Lebesgue covering dimension on C_p, not a theta count (TAA Lemma 147, correction 1).

concepts.name: Width → area → 2-form: (1/2π)Δ log|ξ| dσ∧dt = Σ δ_ρ
concepts.plain: A zero’s line always has area π however wide it is; stacking these areas over the strip gives the 2-form that counts zeros, and RH would need that count to come from a positive pairing.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: [T] Re ξ′/ξ(σ+it) = ∂_σ log|ξ|; each line has area π·sgn(σ−β) independent of its width (width × height = 1); crossing σ = β the area jumps by 2π = flux of ∇log|ξ| around ρ; Poincaré–Lelong/Jensen: (1/2π)Δ log|ξ| dσ∧dt = Σ_ρ δ_ρ (BIB). [N] TAA Lemma 154 fitted amplitudes = 1 to ≤ 3.4e−5 (area π); DH ghost-1 near amplitude −1 at d = 0.30, +1 at d = 0.35. [R] Pairing the 2-form with test functions = zero side of Weil's explicit formula; making it positive = MP4. Local areas are ghost-blind in total; their sign seen from σ > ½ is ghost-sensitive.

concepts.name: Automorphy defect (TAA Lemma 144)

concepts.name: Dual conic (adjugate): ellipse ↔ ellipse, hyperbola ↔ hyperbola, line pair ↔ double point
concepts.plain: The family of tangent lines of a conic is itself a conic; for a pair of crossing lines it collapses to the crossing point, counted twice.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: The tangent lines of a nondegenerate conic xᵀMx = 0 (3×3) form the dual conic uᵀM⁻¹u = 0 (equivalently adj M). For the affine block xᵀAx = 1: dual yᵀA⁻¹y = 1 (same type). A line pair (rank 2 in P²; J. W. McGreevy's pure wedge) has rank-1 adjugate: the dual is the vertex counted twice (claim 4 correct, for the 3×3 projective matrix). Fixes the 'unique absolute definition' of each stratum up to scale.

concepts.name: Morse picture of the strata: lobes (extrema), wedge (saddle level), hyperbolic windows (index 1)
aliases: lobes vs wedges vs hyperbolic windows
concepts.plain: Near a non-degenerate critical point a function looks like a quadratic form: a minimum gives closed elliptical loops (lobes), a saddle gives hyperbolas, and the level through the saddle is a pair of crossing lines (the wedge).
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: [T] Morse lemma: near a non-degenerate critical point f = f(p) ± x² ± y² in suitable coordinates. Index 0 or 2: level sets are closed ellipse-like loops (J. W. McGreevy’s lobes). Index 1: level sets are hyperbolas and the critical level is a crossing line pair (the pure wedge, the dual conic of which is a double point: dual_conic). det Hess = 0 is the degenerate parabolic case (a² = 4q, double line). This is the local version of conic_type_at_infinity, and the block test of blockwise_weil_diagnostic: an off-line pair gives an index-1 (hyperbolic) 2×2 block, a ‘hyperbolic window’ (DH: [84.36,84.77], [85.48,85.91], [114.04,114.29], TAA Lemma 153). [A] Identification with the animation frames.
concepts.uncertain: Chat-level concept; not a lemma result. Morse lemma not opened at source.

concepts.name: Cusp ≠ archimedean place
concepts.plain: The cusp of the modular curve and the archimedean place of ℚ are different objects, though both get written ∞.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: The cusp is a point of the modular curve; the archimedean place is a valuation of ℚ. Neither is the frame bundle, and ∞-toposes are unrelated to the infinite place.

concepts.name: Pole of ζ at s = 1 (residue / 3/π)
concepts.plain: ζ has a pole at s = 1; the Eisenstein series E(z,s) has its pole there with residue 3/π, the reciprocal of the area of the modular surface.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: Res_{s=1} E(z,s) = 3/π = 1/vol(SL₂(ℤ)∖ℍ); E₂* = E₂ − 3/(πy) is the non-holomorphic correction (TAA Lemma 144/TAA Lemma 145 context).

concepts.name: Selberg resonances
concepts.plain: Poles of φ(s) relate to ζ zeros at s = ρ/2.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: φ = Λ(2s−1)/Λ(2s) has poles in Re s < ½ exactly at ρ/2, φ(½) = −1 (TAA Lemma 143). ΣΛ(P)N^{−s} = Z′/Z(s) − Z′/Z(s+1). TAA Lemma 148: per-resonance decay rates read for 79 ρ/2 (γ < 200), all consistent with ¼ (calibration).

concepts.name: Toeplitz / Verblunsky coefficients
concepts.plain: Positivity of Toeplitz matrices ⇔ |α_n| < 1; each step a boost of rapidity artanh|α|.

Levinson: PD ⇔ |κ_j| < 1, each step a boost of rapidity artanh κ (true |κ| < 1 for 60 orders; ghost κ₈ = −1.0009). TAA Lemma 117: U(1,1) boost of velocity |α|; |α| > 1 = Krein swap ∘ boost. TAA Lemma 37/TAA Lemma 118: Schur/Verblunsky layer stripping = restatement (circular).

concepts.name: S-mirror ρ ↦ 1 − ρ̄

concepts.label: Theorem

concepts.name: Arakelov geometry
concepts.plain: Compactified arithmetic surfaces.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 74: Ô(1)² = ½ for FS metrics; pole-plane Gram [[½,1],[1,0]] signature (1,1); Hodge index vacuous in genus 0. TAA Lemma 139: Pic^(Spec ℤ̄) ≅ ℝ has rank 1 and no complex structure. TAA Lemma 65/TAA Lemma 145: Faltings–Hriljac = Hodge index on arithmetic surfaces (curve × Spec O_K), relative part = Néron–Tate, not ζ. TAA Lemma 138 R5: Néron–Tate PD (37a1 ĥ = 0.051114). TAA Lemma 152: Faltings 1984 (Ann. Math. 119, 387–424), Hriljac 1985 (Amer. J. Math. 107, 23–38), bibliographic data verified: Hodge index on arithmetic surfaces ⇒ Néron–Tate positive definite; not RH for any L-function (TAA Lemma 152, correction 12).

concepts.name: Density / volume reading
concepts.plain: The modular surface’s volume form and the half-density: area π/3 gives degree 1/12, and the half-density y^½ is the Heaviside ½ — structure, not sign.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 141 §7: c₁(ω, Pet) = dxdy/(4πy²); area π/3 ⇒ deg ω = 1/12 = −ζ(−1); χ_orb = −1/6; half-density y^½ unitary L²(dr) → L²(dy/y²) = Heaviside ½. TAA Lemma 145: the U-form is indefinite, not a volume (TAA Lemma 145 corrections); volume formula for h⁰ is heuristic.

concepts.name: F₁ base
concepts.plain: The hoped-for "field with one element" under Spec ℤ. Over F₁ the single Frobenius trace becomes a sum over all zeros, and Connes–Consani take the sphere spectrum 𝕊 as F₁.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 65: a_p is the right model, but over F₁ the single trace becomes Σ_ρ u^ρ (one eigenvalue per zero, infinite genus, N(1) = −∞); for curves the CC dictionary is literal (u = qⁿ, α_i = q^{ρ_i}). CC10 N(u) positive on (1,∞) is prime-side and shared by Beurling systems ⇒ cannot force RH alone. TAA Lemma 147, correction 4: "On the metaphysics of F₁" proves no new RR; it restates CC23 and discusses 𝕊 as F₁.
pitfalls: CC N(u) is only formal (TAA Lemma 65 C1).

concepts.name: Principalization
concepts.plain: Making divisors principal; Abel–Jacobi = principalization (TAA Lemma 139).
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 60: "principalization as hamiltonization"; clutching = principalization (analogy). TAA Lemma 71: curve version theorem — #Pic⁰(F_{pⁿ}) = |1 − πⁿ|²; on Spec ℤ only the ℝ>0 boost (blind to θ_p). TAA Lemma 73: class group = obstruction to integral spinor square roots of light rays. TAA Lemma 139: Abel–Jacobi = principalization.

concepts.name: Spec ℤ is terminal
concepts.plain: Spec ℤ has no base to fiber over, unlike a curve over F_q.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Spec ℤ ×_ℤ Spec ℤ = Spec ℤ (TAA Lemma 65 THM), so the "square" must be built elsewhere (arithmetic site, Borger). TAA Lemma 137: Spec ℤ is terminal ⇒ Yoneda gives uniqueness only. TAA Lemma 140: π₁ét(Spec ℤ) = 1.

concepts.name: Spinor/Clifford route
concepts.plain: Encode J and F as a Clifford pair; ghosts give the indefinite Cl(1,1).
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 101/TAA Lemma 110: ghosts give Cl(1,1); true case Cl(2,0).

concepts.name: Weil Rosetta stone
concepts.plain: Weil’s analogy number fields / function fields / Riemann surfaces.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 140: Rosetta table (loop, H¹, 1 ⊕ 𝕃, counts, involution, sign); the Spec ℤ sign cell is missing (Weil positivity ⇔ RH). Column 2’s sign is the dim-2 algebraic shadow of Hodge–Riemann (surface + ample + RR ⇒ Hodge index). Weil’s 1940 letter quotes read at source (Krieger, Notices 52(3)).

concepts.name: Cohesion (arena)
concepts.plain: Cohesion is the arena, not the surface.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 141 §3: cohesion is the arena, not the surface; the étale ∞-topos of Spec ℤ is not cohesive (pro-shape, Hoyois); new Thm: [ℕ^×, Set] is not cohesive (Γ has no right adjoint). D10 (relative cohesion). TAA Lemma 146 §5: the cohesion quadruple Π ⊣ Disc ⊣ Γ ⊣ coDisc is a line without sign; RLGC is a 2×2 grid with mirror/KK/sign — numerology only.

concepts.name: Local-to-global failure
concepts.plain: Local positivity at each prime does not imply global.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 25 Rem 6.2: naive local positivity fails (K < 0 for |r| < 6.28984); CC21 Thm 1 local archimedean positivity only for supp ⊂ [2^{−½}, 2^{½}] with vanishing. TAA Lemma 64/TAA Lemma 65: local Hasse (Q_p > 0 at every p, proved) vs global RH for L(E,s) (open) — the collective split. TAA Lemma 66: local positivity via Deligne weights is ghost-blind residual data.

concepts.name: Kramers–Kronig relations
concepts.plain: Causal response: real (dispersive) and imaginary (absorptive) parts determine each other. Absorption’s sign is the passivity condition.
concepts.label: Analogy
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 146: dispersion = phase (ghost-blind), absorption sign = passivity ⇔ Lagarias ⇔ RH. TAA Lemma 154: for ξ′/ξ on a line σ: Im = −H[Re] + Σ_{β>σ} −2(t−γ)/((σ−β)²+(t−γ)²) [T]; FFT check on DH/ζ models (zeros |γ−100| < 40, t ∈ [−1900, 2100]): residual ≤ 1e−4 when no zero is right of σ; DH ghost term recovered to ≤ 9.5e−5. KK alone is an identity either way (TAA Lemma 146, correction 3); the sign of Re carries RH.
pitfalls: Passivity implies causality, not conversely (TAA Lemma 146).

concepts.name: Gribov ambiguity
concepts.plain: In QCD the gluon propagator violates positivity (it changes sign in Euclidean time) — the physics example of a "spectral weight" that is not positive.
concepts.label: Analogy
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 146 §3: Gribov C(t) re-derived to 1e−16, first sign change t* = π/(2√2 M) = 1.1107 (in units of M). Interpretation as positivity violation is interpretive (TAA Lemma 146 corrections).
pitfalls: Gluon positivity violation as confinement evidence is interpretive (TAA Lemma 146 corrections).

concepts.name: Half Tate twist ℚ(½)
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: ℚ(1) cyclotomic, H² = ℚ(−1); ℚ(½) not canonical: ℓ-adic F(½) needs a chosen √p (Katz–Rojas-León, opened); g_p² = (−1/p)p gives canonical √(p*) ∈ ℚ(ζ_p); √p for p ≡ 3 mod 4 costs √−1 (disc ℚ(√p) = 4p: ramified at 2; p* < 0: sign at ∞). Over ℝ canonical: Connes's E(f)(g) = |g|^{½} Σ f(qg) and C(1) = (j,λ) ↦ |j|λ. Two product formulas: ∏|x|_v = 1 (size: norm map, scaling flow, √ = critical line) vs ∏(a,b)_v = 1 (phase, obstruction at 2). HEURISTIC nexus: Deninger's cohomology contains an honest ℚ(½), MP4 stated on H¹(½); all twist data ghost-blind.

concepts.name: Functional equation ξ(s) = ξ(1 − s)
concepts.plain: ζ’s completed version is symmetric under s ↦ 1 − s. Ghosts satisfy it too, so it cannot prove RH.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: ξ(s) = ξ(1 − s); DH satisfies FE to 5×10⁻¹⁵ yet Re ξ′/ξ = −66.8 off the line (TAA Lemma 146). Ghost-blind.
pitfalls: Symmetry is phase data, never sign.

concepts.name: Gauss-sum unitarity |g| = √p (RH for a CM curve as a unitarity identity)
concepts.plain: A quadratic Gauss sum has absolute value exactly √p: this is the statement that the finite Fourier transform is unitary. For the CM curve y² = x³ − x and p ≡ 1 mod 4, the Frobenius eigenvalue is a Gaussian integer π with ππ̄ = p, so RH for this curve is the same kind of unitarity identity.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: |g|² = p (checked numerically for all odd p ≤ 691) = Plancherel for the finite Fourier transform, the same |x|^{½} twist as TAA Lemma 145. For p ≡ 1 mod 4, π ∈ ℤ[i], ππ̄ = p, a_p = 2 Re π, so |α| = √p is automatic. Over ℚ the analogue |ε| = 1 of a root number holds for Davenport–Heilbronn too: necessary, not sufficient. Open: a ζ-analogue in which the eigenvalue itself is a Gauss sum.
concepts.formula: |g|² = p, ππ̄ = p, a_p = 2 Re π
pitfalls: Unitarity identities of this kind are Ax3 (phase); over ℚ they are satisfied by DH too and cannot replace the sign.

concepts.name: Nash–Kuiper flexibility / Onsager threshold
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: No 'Nash–Kuiper transform': Nash 1954 / Kuiper 1955 C¹ isometric embeddings (flat torus in ℝ³, crumpled sphere); rigidity of convex surfaces for C^{1,α}, α > 2/3 (Borisov; Cohn-Vossen, Herglotz, Pogorelov for C²); h-principle α < 1/(1+n+n²) (CDS), 1/5 for 2D disks (DIS); threshold open in [1/5, 2/3] (½ suggested). Onsager 1/3 settled (CET 1994; Isett; BDLSV 2019). Cao–Hirsch–Inauen 1/3⁻ is Monge–Ampère, not isometric. ANALOGY: DH = the Nash–Kuiper surface (FE + phases, no Frobenius/H¹/cup ⇒ zeros unpinned).

concepts.name: Half turn = sign flip (S² = −I, root number, Hardy Z sign changes)
concepts.plain: Turning by 180° is a sign: it flips modular forms of odd weight, gives the root number, and is the sign change of Hardy’s Z at each zero on the line.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: S² = −I in SL₂(ℤ) acts by (−1)^k on weight k (odd weights vanish; weight ½ needs the metaplectic cover). s ↦ 1 − s is the 180° rotation about ½; its sign is the root number (+1 for ζ, −1 for 37a1, forcing L(E,1) = 0). Hardy Z(t) = e^{iϑ(t)} ζ(½ + it) is real; it changes sign at each on-line zero of odd order. An off-line pair adds 2 to N(T) and no sign change. TAA Lemma 152 NUM (t ∈ [10,120], step 0.01): ζ 38 sign changes / 38 zeros; DH 62 / 66, the two deficits of 2 exactly in [80,90] and [110,120] (off-line pairs 85.699, 114.163). ℝP¹ = directions mod 180°; tautological bundle = Möbius band (the sign).
numbers: DH: 62 sign changes vs N = 66; 5 vs 7 on [80,90] and [110,120]
pitfalls: Ghost-blind at on-line zeros (DH flips like ζ); off-line zeros appear only as missing flips against a global count N(T) (argument principle, Turing-type): detection, not positivity (TAA Lemma 152, correction 8).

concepts.name: Archimedean place and Γ_ℝ factor
concepts.plain: The "prime at infinity": its Gamma factor contributes a term to the Weil form that can be positive or negative depending on the window.
