concepts.name: Connes–Consani 2021: Weil positivity at the archimedean place (support [2^{−1/2}, 2^{1/2}])
concepts.plain: Connes and Consani explain why Weil’s form is positive for test functions too narrow to see the prime 2: it dominates a trace on Sonin space.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: Selecta Math. (N.S.) 27 (2021) no. 4, art. 77 (arXiv 2006.13771, opened). Weil's inequality: f smooth positive definite, supp f ⊂ (1/2, 2), f̂(±i/2) = 0 ⇒ W∞(f) ≥ 0 (proved by Yoshida 1992 by explicit computation); ⇔ QW(g) = W∞(g∗g*) ≥ 0 for supp g ⊂ [2^{−1/2}, 2^{1/2}], ĝ(i/2) = 0. Support (1/2,2) chosen so that no rational prime enters. Thm 1: if also ĝ(0) = 0, W∞(g∗g*) ≥ Tr(ϑ(g) S ϑ(g)*), S = projection on Sonin space; Thm 6.11: without ĝ(0) = 0, ≥ Tr(...) − c|ĝ(0)|², 13 < c < 17. Their abstract method alone reaches I = [u⁻¹,u], u = 1.10246 (Cor 8) / 1.15077 (Rem 9); [1/2,2] needs Sonin/prolate and numerics (§6). In log scale: f supported in |u| < log 2 = the first prime atom; TAA Lemma 25's OS-RP fails exactly when the atom log 2 enters. Ghost-blind (archimedean only).

concepts.name: Cusp forms & Petersson positivity
concepts.plain: Cusp forms have positive Petersson norm — a real positivity, but it does not see ζ’s zeros.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: ⟨f,f⟩ = ∫|f|²y^k dμ > 0; HR = 2 × Petersson (TAA Lemma 134). Ghost-blind for ζ (TAA Lemma 146).
pitfalls: Positive but about cusp forms, not ζ’s spectral weights.

concepts.name: E₂ anomaly (E₂* = E₂ − 3/(πy))
concepts.plain: E₂ fails to be modular; fixing it costs a non-holomorphic term 3/(πy) tied to the pole. One reading treats the failure as a 2-class.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: E₂(−1/z) = z²E₂(z) + 12z/(2πi)… corrected by E₂* = E₂ − 3/(πy), modular of weight 2. Ghost-blind (phase/automorphy data).
concepts.uncertain: Exact transformation constant quoted from standard theory; the 2-class reading is conjectural.

concepts.name: Euler characteristic χ(D) = dim H⁰ − dim H¹ (Connes–Consani RR)
concepts.plain: The χ in the Connes–Consani Riemann–Roch is an Euler characteristic: sections minus obstructions of a divisor D. It is a number attached to D, not a character of a Galois group.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: CC23 over 𝕊: χ(D) = dim H⁰(D) − dim H¹(D) = ⌈deg₂D⌉′ + 1 (TAA Lemma 147). TAA Lemma 145 parity: a linear χ is odd in D and never contains D²; the Hodge-index step needs a quadratic χ (D²/2 term). TAA Lemma 147: χ(D) + χ(−D) = 2 (deg₂D ∉ ℤ).
pitfalls: Notation clash: this χ is an Euler characteristic, not the character χ (or ω) of the 691 class-group eigenspace.

concepts.name: Herbrand–Ribet: ω¹⁻ᵏ eigenspace of Cl(ℚ(μ_p)) and p | B_k
concepts.plain: The p-part of the class group of ℚ(μ_p) splits into pieces labelled by powers of the Teichmüller character ω. The piece ω¹⁻ᵏ is nonzero exactly when p divides the Bernoulli number B_k; for p = 691, k = 12 this is the ω⁻¹¹ piece.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: For odd p and even k, 2 ≤ k ≤ p−3: A(ω¹⁻ᵏ) ≠ 0 ⇔ p | B_k (Herbrand 1932 ⇒, Ribet 1976 ⇐). p = 691, k = 12: B₁₂ = −691/2730, class in ω⁻¹¹ = ωᵖ⁻¹² (same character, since ω has order p − 1); odd character ⇒ minus part. TAA Lemma 66: 691 has two irregular indices (12, 200), so Cl/691 is 2-dim (ω⁻¹¹, ω⁻¹⁹⁹); ρ_{Δ,691} ss = 1 ⊕ ω¹¹, the non-split extension gives the ω⁻¹¹ class via CFT (Greenberg–Monsky lattices).
pitfalls: Notation: det ρ_Δ = χ_cyc¹¹ (cyclotomic character), whose reduction mod 691 is ω¹¹; the class itself sits in ω⁻¹¹ (TAA Lemma 66).
Ribet 1976 used weight-2 forms on Γ₁(p), not Δ.
Some authors write ωᵖ⁻¹²; it is the same eigenspace.

rels.note: size statement implied by the main conjecture
sizes, not signs: ghost-blind residual data (TAA Lemma 66)

concepts.name: Mazur–Wiles main conjecture ("Euler characteristic = L-value")
concepts.plain: The size of each Teichmüller piece of the class group (and of the Iwasawa module up the cyclotomic tower) equals the p-part of an L-value; slogan: an algebraic Euler characteristic equals an analytic L-value.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: Mazur–Wiles 1984: characteristic ideal of the χ-part of the Iwasawa module = ideal of the Kubota–Leopoldt p-adic L-function. Finite-level consequence: #A(ω¹⁻ᵏ) = p-part of L(0, ωᵏ⁻¹) (Ribet, Berkeley slides). TAA Lemma 66: main conjecture = Hilbert–Pólya-type with free p-adic unitarity (γ eigenvalues are 1-units); μ = 0 is not a positivity; no positivity found on the Iwasawa side (OPEN).
pitfalls: Iwasawa theory measures sizes (orders, characteristic ideals), never the sign of D²; it cannot by itself give Weil positivity.
"Euler characteristic = L-value" is a slogan (Heuristic wording), the theorem is the equality of ideals.

concepts.name: Tate count / Picard number (ghost-blind)
concepts.plain: Counting algebraic classes on C×C does not see whether eigenvalues are on the circle.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: ρ(C×C) = 2 + Σ m(λ)m(q/λ) (Tate 1966, S–S §14.6); = 2g for squarefree, fakes too (TAA Lemma 93 Prop 2.3).

concepts.name: Consani: archimedean cohomology, N at infinity, Γ-factor as a characteristic polynomial
concepts.plain: At the infinite place there is a proved cohomology whose Frobenius has the Gamma factor as characteristic polynomial; it is purely local.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: Consani, Compositio 111 (1998) 323–358 (abstract read): a double complex with a monodromy-type operator N at the archimedean fibre, viewed as 'maximally degenerate' (analogue of LMHS); proves Deninger's conjecture that the archimedean Γ-factor is the (regularized) characteristic polynomial of an archimedean Frobenius on the N-invariants of the hypercohomology. Local only: says nothing about zeros (ghost-blind: DH has the Γ-factor of an odd character mod 5).

concepts.name: Ramanujan congruence τ(n) ≡ σ₁₁(n) mod 691 (Δ ≡ E₁₂)
concepts.plain: The cusp form Δ agrees with the Eisenstein series E₁₂ modulo 691, because 691 divides the numerator of ζ(−11). It is the meeting point of the Eisenstein (reference) and cusp-form (primitive) parts of the Hecke algebra.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: τ(n) ≡ σ₁₁(n) mod 691; ζ(−11) = −B₁₂/12 = 691/32760 (constant term of E₁₂ ∝ ζ(−11)/2 = 691/65520, TAA Lemma 70). TAA Lemma 66: τ(p) ≡ 1 + p¹¹ mod 691 for all 9592 p < 10⁵; Hecke congruence moduli N_k = |num(B_k/2k)| = 691, 3617, 43867, … (k = 12, 16, 18, …); bridge = closed point where Eisenstein and cuspidal components of Spec 𝕋 meet. TAA Lemma 70 (Mazur77 at source): Eisenstein ideal 𝕋/𝔍 ≅ ℤ/n, modulus = numerator of an Euler-depleted ζ(1−k); cusp encodes it as a negative zeta value; positivity invisible (timelike f ≡ spacelike E).
pitfalls: The congruence is mod 691 data: it says nothing about the sign of the Weil form (TAA Lemma 66: bridge = where positivity is lost).
E₁₂ has all its zeros off Re s = 6 (unconditional, TAA Lemma 66) — an "all ghost" Euler product.

rels.note: weight-12 rung: E₁₂ reference vs Δ primitive
Eisenstein = reference, cusp form = primitive split

concepts.name: Hecke operators
concepts.plain: Averaging operators on modular forms; self-adjointness gives real eigenvalues but not the Ramanujan bound.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Hecke self-adjoint ⇒ a_p ∈ ℝ, not |a_p| ≤ 2√p (TAA Lemma 134). Ghost-blind (TAA Lemma 146).
pitfalls: a_p are not BSD generators.

concepts.name: Bost–Connes KMS states
concepts.plain: A quantum statistical system whose partition function is ζ(β); its positive KMS states and phase transition at β = 1 see ζ only at real β > 1, never the zeros.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: BC95 (Thm 5; CM08 3.32): Q-structure, Gal(Q^cycl/Q) symmetry, positive KMS states, ζ(β) real for β > 1; no trace equal to the Weil distribution found (TAA Lemma 30). TAA Lemma 38: strongest rigorous bridge; BC time is dual to rapidity, (β,t) = (Re s, −Im s); BC ordered phase ⇔ ω > ½. TAA Lemma 39: BC = tensor product over primes twisted by Galois. TAA Lemma 54/TAA Lemma 118: KMS/passivity uses ζ at real β > 1 ⇒ ghost-blind.
pitfalls: BC95 Thm 5(a) states β < 1 (β ≤ 1 from CM08 3.32) (TAA Lemma 38 flag).

concepts.name: Primary sign rule for a_p of y² = x³ − x
concepts.plain: For p ≡ 1 mod 4 write p = a² + b² with b even; the sign of a in a_p = 2a is fixed by a 2-adic normalisation (a + b ≡ 1 mod 4). The individual sign is phase data; RH is about the size |a_p| ≤ 2√p, not the sign.
concepts.label: Numerical
concepts.core: p = a² + b², b even, a_p = 2a with a + b ≡ 1 mod 4 (π primary mod (1 + i)³); checked for all 14 primes p ≡ 1 mod 4 below 120 (p = 5, 13, 17: a_p = −2, 6, 2). The individual sign is a 2-adic phase (ghost-blind); RH = |a_p| ≤ 2√p is a size statement. The distribution of the signs (Sato–Tate for CM curves) is a separate question; no citation given here. TAA Lemma 150 Prop 3.3: checked on all 147 primes ≡ 1 mod 4 below 2000. Individual sign = 2-adic phase (ghost-blind); the averaged sign is the Sarnak bias 1 − 2r (TAA Lemma 150 §2.1). CM angles: χ² = 0.34 on 10 bins (n = 39,175, p < 1e6), 50.07% positive; Hecke/Deuring equidistribution [BIB, not opened].
concepts.formula: a_p = 2a, p = a² + b², a + b ≡ 1 mod 4
concepts.uncertain: Sato–Tate/Hecke–Deuring citation for CM sign distribution not verified; none given.
pitfalls: The minus sign in a₅ = −2 is not the positivity sign of RH: it is a phase (choice of primary generator), and RH bounds the size.

rels.note: the sign of a_p is not the Castelnuovo sign

concepts.name: Maass–Selberg relations
concepts.plain: Norm of truncated Eisenstein series expressed via φ and φ′; positivity there is automatic.
concepts.label: Numerical
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 146 §8.1: Maass–Selberg ‖Λ^T E‖² minimum 0.611 (ζ) vs 1.383 (DH) over 540 points ⇒ ghost-blind; it only constrains ζ(w) ≠ 0 for Re w > 1 (already known). TAA Lemma 153 (G): on s = ½+it, ‖Λ^T E‖² = 2 log T − (φ′/φ)(½+it) + (φ̄T^{2it} − φT^{−2it})/(2it) (form as in TAA Lemma 69, checked there to ≤ 1.9e−15 by quadrature against Sarnak's (25)); a line in log T with slope 2 and intercept −φ′/φ(½+it) (J. W. McGreevy's y-intercepts). The intercept is not a positive density: −φ′/φ(½+it) = −1.907 at t = 0.5, −0.135 at t = 2, +0.005 at t = 3 (TAA Lemma 153, correction 23). Positivity reaches only the edge Re s = 1 (TAA Lemma 69).

concepts.name: Archimedean thresholds a*
concepts.plain: Largest window size where the archimedean part alone is positive.
concepts.label: Numerical
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 127: a*_S2 < 0.5976773 (supersedes TAA Lemma 121’s 0.602); TAA Lemma 98 states a ≤ 1 in another normalization. Ghost-blind.
concepts.uncertain: Normalization between TAA Lemma 98 and TAA Lemma 127 not reconciled here.
pitfalls: Source conflict: TAA Lemma 98 "a ≤ 1" vs TAA Lemma 127 a* < 0.5976773 (different setups/normalizations to check).

concepts.name: Metaplectic / Kubota cocycle
concepts.plain: A 2-valued cocycle on SL₂ behind half-integer weight; structure without sign.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 146 §4: Kubota cocycle is a phase (Ax3); Hilbert product formula 300/300, quadratic reciprocity; θ weight ½ is metaplectic (a fourth root, TAA Lemma 141 §7) — mod 2 data, ghost-blind. TAA Lemma 151: θ multiplier eighth roots = Weil index; local covers split over SL₂(ℤ_p), p odd [BIB]; obstruction at 2 and ∞ = half-twist ±1.

concepts.name: Half-density normalization |x|^{½}
aliases: critical line = spectrum of unitary scaling
concepts.plain: Multiplying by |x|^{½} makes scaling unitary on L²; this is why the critical line is at ½.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 145 Thm twist: |x|^½ = (dx/d*x)^½ is unitary L²(dx) → L²(d*x); U_λ unitary with generator −(x∂_x + ½); Mellin is unitary only on Re s = ½ (Plancherel 0.35355339 both sides; at Re 0.4 a weighted norm 0.53173). Cusp gauge y²∂²(y^½W) = y^½(W″ − W/4). TAA Lemma 153 (E): (U_λ f)(x) = λ^{½}f(λx) on L²(ℝ₊,dx): U_λ x^{−s} = λ^{½−s} x^{−s} (NUM ≤ 2.2e−16), |λ^{½−s}| = 1 for all λ iff Re s = ½ (x^{−s} is a generalized eigenfunction, not in L²). Critical line = unitary spectrum of scaling; this is unitarity (Ax3), not positivity.
pitfalls: There are two ½’s (TAA Lemma 145 corrections): the unitary twist and the critical line.

concepts.name: Theta inversion θ(1/t) = √t θ(t)
concepts.plain: Poisson summation gives the functional equation; phase data.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: θ(1/x) = √x θ(x) gives Riemann’s FE and the boundary terms f(0), f̂(0) of 1/(s(s−1)) (TAA Lemma 36 §6). TAA Lemma 138 R4: theta inversion for x² + 5y² to 3e−30; Weil representation unitary, (ST)³ = Gauss sum · I; unitarity ⇒ FE only, ghost-blind (Thm). TAA Lemma 145: θ FE error 6.3e−26; TAA Lemma 146: θ S-error ≤ 2.5e−16, Fresnel = half-density × Weil index. TAA Lemma 151 centrepiece: θ(1/t) = √t θ(t) and ϑ(−1/τ) = √(τ/i) ϑ(τ) to ≤1.5e−51; √(1/i) = (1 − i)/√2 primitive 8th root (√2 in the phase); t^{¼}θ(t) inversion-invariant; unitary inversion on L²(ℝ₊,dx) is x^{−1}f(1/x) (TAA Lemma 151, correction 6). TAA Lemma 153: √(1/i) = e^{−iπ/4} is the Maslov factor of a negative-definite Hessian (stationary phase).

concepts.name: The prime 2 as the wild place
concepts.plain: The only even prime is 2 (not √2). At 2 the Gauss halves break: (p − 1)/2 is not an integer, every model y² = f(x) has bad reduction, and the Hilbert symbol / metaplectic cocycle is wild. √2 enters through (2/p), which depends on p mod 8.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Supplementary law: (2/p) = +1 ⇔ p ≡ ±1 mod 8; √2 ∈ ℚ(ζ₈), so (2/p) is the character χ₈ (the √2 family). At p = 2, (p − 1)/2 is not an integer and every Weierstrass model y² = f(x) is bad at 2; the Hilbert symbol and the metaplectic (Kubota) cocycle are wild at 2. All of this is phase data, hence ghost-blind.
pitfalls: The even prime is 2, not √2; √2 appears only through the character (2/p) = χ₈(p).
√2 is not a prime (TAA Lemma 150, correction 1); √2 enters via χ₈ and, separately, via Goldfeld's √2 (prime squares).

rels.note: wild at 2: Hilbert symbol / Kubota cocycle

concepts.name: Scattering unitarity |φ| = 1
concepts.plain: The cusp scattering coefficient has modulus one on the critical line — true with or without RH.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: |φ(½ + it)| = 1 follows from the functional equation; it is Ax3 (adjoint) only and ghost-blind.
pitfalls: Not Rosati: only the ππ† = q half.

concepts.name: Fundamental domain of SL₂(ℤ): elliptic (CM points), parabolic (cusp), hyperbolic (closed geodesics)
concepts.plain: The modular surface has two cone points, one cusp and many closed geodesics: the three kinds of motion seen on the quotient.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Elliptic points i (stabilizer ⟨S⟩) and ρ = e^{2πi/3} (⟨ST⟩) = CM points of discriminant −4, −3; one cusp (0 = S·∞ ~ i∞ for SL₂(ℤ); for Γ₀(N) the cusps 0 and ∞ are distinct, swapped by the Fricke involution); hyperbolic classes ↔ closed geodesics of length 2 log ε (Selberg's primes). Interior: Δ ≥ 0 (selberg_eigenvalue_mass_shell); cusp: unitary scattering φ (eisenstein_resonances_rho_half); CM points: Epstein/Hecke (epstein). The cusp ties them: its constant term carries ζ.

rels.note: cusp is a point, not the place ∞

concepts.name: Hilbert reciprocity at 2: the odd halves become sign bits
concepts.plain: At odd primes the halves (p − 1)/2 count squares; at 2 the corresponding quantities ε(u) = (u − 1)/2 and ω(u) = (u² − 1)/8 are sign bits. Hilbert reciprocity says the sign at 2 is fixed by the odd places and ∞. This is phase information, not positivity.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: (−1/p) = (−1)^{ε(p)}, (2/p) = (−1)^{ω(p)}. 2-adic Hilbert symbol: for a = 2^α u, b = 2^β v with u, v odd units, (a,b)₂ = (−1)^{ε(u)ε(v) + αω(v) + βω(u)} (Serre, A Course in Arithmetic, Ch. III, Thm 1). Product formula ∏ᵥ (a,b)ᵥ = 1 over all places including ∞ ⇒ the 2-adic sign is determined by the odd places and ∞; it is a restatement of quadratic reciprocity with both supplementary laws. ℚ₂^×/squares has order 8; ℤ₂^×/squares = {±1, ±5} has order 4: two sign bits, ε (sign of −1) and ω (the √2 / χ₈ bit). Checked: product formula holds for 3000 random pairs |a|, |b| ≤ 5000; ε, ω for u = 1, 3, 5, 7: (0,0), (1,1), (0,1), (1,0). Phase data (Ax3), ghost-blind: Davenport–Heilbronn shares the same reciprocity.
numbers: Serre III Thm 1 formula vs PARI hilbert: 3000/3000
concepts.uncertain: to verify: Serre, A Course in Arithmetic, Ch. III Thm 1 not opened here; formula re-checked numerically via the product formula only.
pitfalls: The sign at 2 is a reciprocity sign (phase), not the positivity sign of RH; reading it as the half-density counterpart is an analogy.
Equivalent to quadratic reciprocity, not to RH.
Phase data: DH obeys the same reciprocity (TAA Lemma 150, correction 2).

rels.note: odd halves (p ± 1)/2 ↔ sign bits ε, ω at 2
Hilbert symbol = the cocycle behind the metaplectic cover

concepts.name: Counts vs quadratic positivity
concepts.plain: Point counts being positive does not force RH; only quadratic forms can.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 109: 2935 count-positive ghosts (g = 2, q = 11).

concepts.name: Eisenstein constant term & scattering φ(s)
concepts.plain: The Eisenstein series’ constant term has two pieces linked by φ(s); on Re s = ½ |φ| = 1 for any zeros — a phase statement.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: φ(s) = ξ(2s−1)/ξ(2s); |φ(½+it)| = 1 unconditionally (unitarity of scattering). Ghost-blind.
pitfalls: |φ| = 1 is only Ax3.

concepts.name: Gauss half: quadratic character, (p ± 1)/2 and the (p + 1)/4 square-root formula
concepts.plain: Every odd prime p splits the nonzero residues into (p − 1)/2 squares and (p − 1)/2 non-squares; the quadratic character (x/p) records which. For an elliptic curve y² = f(x), a_p is minus the sum of these characters, and its value mod p is a Gauss-half power.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: a_p = −Σ_x (f(x)/p) for y² = f(x); Hasse: a_p ≡ coefficient of x^{p−1} in f^{(p−1)/2} mod p. For p ≡ 3 mod 4, (p + 1)/4 is an integer and √a = a^{(p+1)/4} mod p (691 → 173). y² = x³ − x: a_p = −2, 6, 2 for p = 5, 13, 17; a_p = 0 for p ≡ 3 mod 4, so N₆₉₁ = 692. The Gauss halves see only the coherent H¹(E, 𝒪), i.e. a_p mod p; the bound |a_p| ≤ 2√p needs positivity (Castelnuovo/Hodge index). TAA Lemma 150 Prop 3.1 (THM+NUM): verified for p = 3,5,7,11,13,17,29,37,41,691; 70,563 square roots a^{(p+1)/4} and a_p = 0 for p ≡ 3 mod 4, p < 2000. The half records a_p mod p (Hasse invariant = Frobenius on coherent H¹); the bound needs positivity (TAA Lemma 150 Thm 2.2).
pitfalls: a_p mod p is phase-type information; it does not give the size bound |a_p| ≤ 2√p.
The ½ of (p ± 1)/2 is a counting half; relating it to the half-density ½ is an analogy.

rels.note: the ½ in (p ± 1)/2 vs the unitary |x|^{½} twist; analogy
mod-p data cannot give the size bound; that needs Castelnuovo–Severi
the square root sits here; the inequality does not (TAA Lemma 150)

concepts.name: Gauss sum as canonical √(±p)
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: g_p = Σ (x/p) e^{2πix/p}: g_p² = (−1/p)p (NUM to 3.7e−48 for p < 200); g_p = √p (p ≡ 1) or i√p (p ≡ 3 mod 4) (Gauss's sign); so √(p*) is canonical in ℚ(ζ_p) given ψ; Katz–Rojas-León/Katz–Tiep use the Gauss sum as the half-twist constant.

concepts.name: Legendre ↔ Fourier: stationary phase, half-density amplitude, Maslov phase
concepts.plain: The Fourier transform of a wave is, to leading order, its Legendre transform in the phase, a half-density in the amplitude, and a quarter-turn sign for each concave direction.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: ∫e^{i(S(x)−px)}dx ≈ √(2π)|S″(x_p)|^{−½} e^{−iS*(p)} e^{iπ sgn S″/4}, S′(x_p) = p, S*(p) = p x_p − S(x_p) (critical-value Legendre transform); exact for quadratic S (Fresnel). Tangent of slope p meets the y-axis at S − xS′ = −S*(p): the intercepts give the phase; the half-density |dx|^{½} → |dp|^{½} gives the amplitude |S″|^{−½}; the Maslov factor records the Hessian signature and jumps at caustics (S″ = 0), where stationary phase fails (Airy; TAA Lemma 153 NUM). TAA Lemma 153 NUM: rel. err 0.012 (λ=20), 0.003 (λ=80), both signs. e^{−iπ/4} = √(1/i) is the factor in ϑ(−1/τ) = √(τ/i)ϑ(τ) (TAA Lemma 151; 9e−17). Riemann–Siegel θ(t) = (t/2)log(t/2π) − t/2 − π/8 + 1/(48t) + … (NUM); −π/8 as a Maslov-type phase is Heuristic.
pitfalls: Intercepts give the phase, not the half-density; the amplitude comes from the curvature S″ (TAA Lemma 153, correction 15).
Hörmander / Guillemin–Sternberg: bibliographic data only (unopened).

concepts.name: Weight ladder (modular weights)
concepts.plain: Modular forms come in weights; at each rung the Eisenstein series E_k is the reference. A “stratification” of modular structures is this ladder.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 146 corrections: stratification = weight ladder, with E_k the reference per rung; cusp positivity on each rung is ghost-blind. TAA Lemma 139 weight-1 search: weight-1 modular = motivic weight 0 (η(z)η(23z), |α| = 1); motivic weight 1 = weight-2 cusp forms (11a, Rosati PD); ζ appears only in Eisenstein lines (ζ_K weight 1, ζ(s)ζ(s−1) weight 2), not in L².

rels.note: cusp positivity per rung is ghost-blind

concepts.name: Yoshida window positivity
concepts.plain: For test functions supported in a small enough window, Weil positivity holds unconditionally.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: Yoshida: W ≥ 0 for supp f ⊂ small window; TAA Lemma 10 window ≤ log 3. Below ghost onsets, so ghost-blind. TAA Lemma 153: CC21 credit Yoshida (ASPM 21, 1992, 281–325) with W∞(f) ≥ 0 for supp f ⊂ (1/2,2), f̂(±i/2) = 0, i.e. |log x| < log 2 (before the prime 2).
pitfalls: Unconditional windows never reach ghost onset.
Atlas window ≤ log 3 (TAA Lemma 10) vs CC21/Yoshida (1/2, 2) ↔ log 2: different statements/normalizations, not reconciled here.

concepts.name: w₂ / Čech class (TAA Lemma 138)
concepts.plain: Obstruction class to a spin structure, tested as a candidate arithmetic object (TAA Lemma 138).
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 138: the Čech 2-class (polarization, c₁) supplies the pairing, † and Ax3 (π*L ≅ L^q) for free; spin supplies mod-2 refinements only; the sign is always ampleness. TAA Lemma 141 §7: w₂ = c₁ mod 2; half-densities are canonical (no w₂); w₂ governs half-forms (K^{1/2} = ω weight 1).
pitfalls: w₂ is not for densities (TAA Lemma 141 list).

concepts.name: Sector map w = e^{iπs/2}
concepts.plain: Mapping the critical strip to a 90° sector puts the critical line on the 45° ray; the functional equation becomes w ↦ i/w.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: arg w = πσ/2: strip edges σ = 0, 1 → rays 90° apart, critical line → the 45° ray. s ↦ 1 − s is w ↦ i/w (reflection in the 45° ray composed with |w| ↦ 1/|w|; fixed points ±e^{iπ/4}), not a reflection (TAA Lemma 152, correction 6); the reflection in the 45° ray is s ↦ 1 − s̄, w ↦ i w̄ (NUM 4.5e−28, 4.0e−28). In this picture the 45° ray is the critical line, not a null ray.

concepts.name: Spin structure & theta characteristic
concepts.plain: Theta characteristics = spin structures = square roots of the canonical bundle; they refine the Weil pairing mod 2 and are shared by fakes and true curves alike.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 136: theta chars = spin structures = quadratic refinements of the Weil pairing; Arf counts 3/1, 10/6, 36/28, 136/120, 528/496 (g ≤ 5); K^{1/2} = fixed points of D ↦ K − D = self-dual centre s = ½ [R]. TAA Lemma 138 R3 (exhaustive g ≤ 2): #Frobenius-fixed theta chars = #J[2](F_q); fakes share mod-2 data with true curves ⇒ ghost-blind (Thm). TAA Lemma 141 §7: w₂ governs half-forms (K^{1/2}), not half-densities.
pitfalls: "Spec ℤ not spin": the real place obstructs a half twist — analogy only (TAA Lemma 50 Rem 7.3).

concepts.name: "Cocycles give structure, not sign"
concepts.plain: Any cocycle/class (metaplectic, w₂, defect) fixes structure but cannot decide a positivity sign.
concepts.label: Heuristic
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 138/TAA Lemma 144/TAA Lemma 146 summary principle.

concepts.name: J. W. McGreevy's flat-potential animation: half-turn polarity flip through a pure wedge
concepts.plain: J. W. McGreevy’s animation shows a field turning, passing through a pure wedge and coming back with opposite sign; it is a picture of the sign at each zero.
concepts.label: Heuristic

McGreevy's Aug 2025 GRQFT animation (panel 'Flat Potential Oscillations', 15 stills): the bright region moves clockwise; polarity flips when the pattern passes the 180° side (frames 5→6, 10→11), frame 10 is a pure wedge (constant on rays), a full cycle restores. concepts.name: Purity as distortionless transmission: weight strata = attenuation classes
concepts.plain: On a perfect cable every frequency fades at the same rate; RH-type purity says every Frobenius eigenvalue has the same size, and rescaling by √q makes the fading disappear altogether.
concepts.label: Analogy
concepts.core: Lossless = unitary (|φ| = 1 on the line; after the half-density gauge no attenuation) [T]. Distortionless = every mode shares one attenuation rate [T for the line]. Frobenius eigenvalues |α| = q^{w/2}: α^n decays/grows at rate (w/2) log q, so the weight strata (rings |z| = q^{−σ}) are attenuation classes; purity (one ring) = distortionless [Restatement for Frobenius]; dividing by q^{1/2} (half Tate twist, the e^{−αx} factor) turns distortionless into lossless [T]. For ζ (no Frobenius) this is an Analogy. DH off-line zeros = modes with another attenuation = distortion [R, TAA Lemma 144 overdamped ghost]. Hyperbolic side: characteristics x ± ct are the null lines of dx² − c²dt²; Wick rotation t → iτ makes it dx² + c²dτ² (OS link) — a different sign flip from C → −C in the LC energy (TAA Lemma 153, correction 30). Elliptical conic sections, not elliptic curves. TAA Lemma 154: on the cusp purity = every zero has HWHM pair (¼, ¼), i.e. one lifetime [R]; DH ghost 1 measured (0.0957, 0.4042). On observer lines the FE pairs widths ±Γ (PT gain/loss shape, Analogy).

concepts.name: Buoyancy / Archimedes principle
concepts.plain: Weight is measured relative to the fluid displaced; Castelnuovo–Severi and the pole subtraction can be read the same way.
concepts.label: Analogy
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 146 §7: C–S as D² = 2ab + D′² — Archimedes relative to U; the sign is an input (fluids), proved (curves), ⇔ RH (ζ). Buoyancy sign as input: TAA Lemma 146 corrections.

concepts.name: Distortionless line R/L = G/C
concepts.plain: Line that transmits without distortion; corresponds to β = ½.
concepts.label: Analogy
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 25/TAA Lemma 143: distortionless ⇔ β = ½. TAA Lemma 153 (sympy): telegrapher V_xx = LC V_tt + (RC+GL)V_t + RG V; gauge V = e^{−μt}w, μ = (R/L+G/C)/2, leaves w_xx − LC w_tt + [(CR−GL)²/(4CL)]w, zero iff R/L = G/C; then V = e^{−αx}F(t − x√(LC)), α = √(RG) (residual 0). Substituting e^{−αx} in the PDE alone does not remove the loss terms (first-order terms remain; TAA Lemma 153, correction 26). Cusp: u = log y, y²∂_y² = ∂_u² − ∂_u, a = e^{u/2}w ⇒ ∂_u² − ¼ (sympy), w = e^{itu} + φe^{−itu} at λ = ¼ + t²: distortionless (k = t, group velocity 1) w.r.t. λ − ¼ (Lax–Phillips shift), Klein–Gordon dispersive w.r.t. λ (v_g = k/√(k²+¼)).

concepts.name: Heaviside RLGC line
concepts.plain: Transmission line with resistance, inductance, conductance, capacitance; used as a model for β.
concepts.label: Analogy
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 25: {R/L, G/C} = {β, 1 − β} in τ, orientation conventional (Prop 3.3); TAA Lemma 143 R/2L ↔ β/2; TAA Lemma 144 unordered {(1−β)/2, β/2} in u. TAA Lemma 153: gauge residual (CR−GL)²/(4CL) recomputed (sympy); the cusp is a distortionless line after the half-density gauge (see distortionless). LC energy ½LI² + ½CV² is an ellipse in (V,I) iff L, C > 0 (Hessian det LC): physical positivity = the input MP4 lacks (Analogy); C < 0 gives the hyperbola, C = 0 the double line.

concepts.name: Higgs mechanism: negative mass² at the symmetric point
concepts.label: Analogy
concepts.core: V = −μ²|φ|² + λ|φ|⁴: mass² = −μ² < 0 at φ = 0 (tachyonic); vacuum |φ|² = μ²/2λ, ⟨φ⟩ = v/√2, v = μ/√λ ≈ 246 GeV; m_H² = 2μ² > 0; Yukawa m_f = y v/√2 (√2 a convention). Positivity by CHOICE of vacuum — RH cannot choose (zeros are given). Mass is not friction (no dissipation, Lorentz invariant; TAA Lemma 150, correction 14). Honest link to GRR/relative counts: main term + oscillation ↔ vev + fluctuation only.
pitfalls: The cusp two-Lorentzian “doublet” (TAA Lemma 153 Thm 7.7, TAA Lemma 154) is a parity doublet, not the Higgs complex doublet: no continuous group, no vev, no eaten modes (TAA Lemma 154, correction 13).

concepts.name: Anomalous dispersion
concepts.plain: Phase behavior near a line; ghost-blind.
concepts.label: Analogy
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 36: anomalous dispersion = analogy — gain lines are where absorption and phase disagree; THM 4.3 absorption–phase sum rule ∫₀ᵀ Re ξ′/ξ(σ₀+it)dt = π[N(T) − 2N(σ₀,T)] + …, deficit 2πN(σ₀,T) ≥ 0 (leads to zero density, not a proof). TAA Lemma 78: causality versus linewidth, Kramers–Kronig for the modular scattering matrix. TAA Lemma 146: dRe χ/dω at centre −6 (absorber) vs +6 (gain). TAA Lemma 154: precise form — per line Im F = −sgn(σ−β) H[Re F]; KK holds on σ iff no zero lies right of σ; a ghost flips the pairing locally (DH residual 9–20 at d = 0.25…0.05, = predicted term to 1e−4; ζ ≤ 1e−4). Re F = group delay d arg ξ/dt, Im F = −d log|ξ|/dt. Convention-free content: relative sign κ = −1/a³ (absorber < 0, gain > 0). J. W. McGreevy's strip prototype (TAA Lemma 36) = this object [R]; 'anomalous' in the optical sense [A].

concepts.name: Lamb cutoff
concepts.plain: In a stratified fluid, waves below the Lamb cutoff frequency c/2H cannot propagate; on the modular surface the cusp’s −¼ is exactly this cutoff with scale height H = 1.
concepts.label: Analogy
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 146 §7: with dy/y² = e^{−r}dr, the cusp −¼ equals the Lamb cutoff c/2H with H = 1 (exact operator identity); TAA Lemma 141 §6: the cusp is a Webster horn A = e^{−r}, Liouville factor e^{r/2}, and +¼ cancels the horn cutoff. Same −¼ as y²∂²(y^½W) = y^½(W″ − W/4) (TAA Lemma 145).
pitfalls: Lamb’s original source not opened (TAA Lemma 146 refs); the identity is checked as an operator identity.

concepts.name: Two different χ’s: Euler characteristic vs class-group character
concepts.plain: The χ of the Connes–Consani Riemann–Roch on the square is an Euler characteristic of a divisor; the χ¹¹ / ω⁻¹¹ of the 691 story is a Galois character labelling an eigenspace. Different objects; any link is an analogy.
concepts.label: Analogy
concepts.core: Euler characteristic χ(D) = dim H⁰ − dim H¹ (TAA Lemma 145/TAA Lemma 147, a number for each divisor) vs Teichmüller / cyclotomic character ω, χ_cyc (TAA Lemma 66, labels of eigenspaces of Cl(ℚ(μ₆₉₁)) and of ρ_Δ mod 691). Shared shape only: Mazur–Wiles equates an algebraic size with an L-value, as RR equates χ with degree + constant. Neither sees the sign of D² (Iwasawa: sizes; CC RR: linear χ).
concepts.uncertain: The analogy itself is interpretive; no TAA lemma relates the two.
pitfalls: Do not identify them: notation clash only.
Iwasawa measures sizes, never the sign of D².
